faqs.question: When in the Diploma should internal assessment support actually begin?
faqs.answer: Earlier than most families start it. The useful window opens when the research question or exploration topic is being chosen, because a weak question limits the marks available no matter how well the writing goes later. In practice that means the middle of DP1 for most subjects. Coming in at the draft stage still helps, since analysis and evaluation sections can be strengthened, but nobody can rescue a poorly framed investigation in the last fortnight. Ask the school for the exact draft date and count backwards from it.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does a DP2 student usually need before the papers?
faqs.answer: It depends on how many subjects are in trouble, and the honest answer is often fewer than parents propose. Two subjects at two sessions each is already four evenings gone, on top of school, homework and the core requirements. Most students do better with one focused weekly session per weak subject plus supervised past-paper practice they complete alone. Adding a fifth or sixth session a week usually reduces independent study time, which is where the marks are actually earned. Review the load every few weeks.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help write the extended essay?
faqs.answer: No, and any tutor offering to is a risk to your child's diploma. The extended essay must be the student's own work, supervised by a school supervisor who signs off on its authenticity. What a tutor can legitimately do is discuss whether the research question is answerable, point out where an argument does not follow, suggest reading, and comment on structure and referencing in the way a supervisor would. The writing, the analysis and the conclusions stay with the student. Keep the school supervisor informed about outside support.

faqs.question: What is TOK support in practice, and can a subject tutor provide it?
faqs.answer: Theory of knowledge asks students to examine how knowledge is produced and justified across different areas, which is unlike anything else on their timetable. Support usually means help unpacking a prescribed title, building an argument with genuine counterclaims, and choosing objects for the exhibition that carry real explanatory weight. A subject specialist in Physics or Economics may be excellent at their subject and poor at this, because the skill is philosophical rather than technical. It is worth asking directly whether a tutor has taught TOK before agreeing to it.

faqs.question: We live in Bestech Park View Sanskruti. Which evening slots are realistically available?
faqs.answer: Slots between roughly four and six in the evening are easiest to fill locally, because a tutor can reach the Sector 48 to 50 belt before the worst of the Sohna Road traffic. Later slots exist but the pool is smaller and travel is unpredictable. Weekend mornings are usually the most reliable for a longer home session. Availability moves through the year as tutors fill their timetables, so a slot that was open in April may not be in September. Online timings are far more flexible.

faqs.question: Is Chemistry HL Paper 3 worth preparing separately?
faqs.answer: Yes, because it tests things the other papers do not. Paper 3 draws on experimental work and on the option content, and students who prepare only through general revision often meet unfamiliar question styles there for the first time in the exam hall. Practical technique, data analysis and the option topic all reward specific preparation. A useful check is to attempt one full past Paper 3 under timed conditions early, then decide how much separate attention it needs. Many students discover the gap is narrower than feared.

faqs.question: What should we expect to see after four weeks of tutoring?
faqs.answer: Not a grade change. Four weeks is too short for that in most subjects, and a tutor claiming otherwise is overselling. What should be visible is a written diagnostic from the first session, a record of topics covered, at least one piece of school-marked work the tutor has read and discussed, and a student who can explain what they are working on without prompting. Attitude usually shifts before marks do. If none of that is present, raise it rather than waiting for the next report.

faqs.question: Do you run group classes or a coaching centre near Sohna Road?
faqs.answer: Sessions arranged through IB Gram are one to one, at home or online, rather than centre-based batches. Group coaching works reasonably for a fixed board syllabus where everyone sits identical papers. It works poorly for the IB, where students in the same room may be on different subject levels, different internal assessment topics and different school deadlines. The value of individual sessions is that the plan follows one student's calendar. Small sibling or shared arrangements are occasionally possible and depend entirely on tutor agreement.

faqs.question: Our son does well in class but drops marks in exams. What changes that?
faqs.answer: Usually timing and command terms rather than knowledge. A student who understands a topic in a relaxed conversation can still lose marks by writing a description where the paper asked them to evaluate, or by spending eighteen minutes on a six-mark question. Work here looks unglamorous: timed sections, mark schemes read line by line, and rewriting answers to match what the command term requires. Improvement tends to appear in mocks rather than immediately. It also fades if timed practice stops, so it needs maintaining.

Support usually means help unpacking a prescribed title, building an argument with genuine counterclaims, and choosing objects for the exhibition that carry real explanatory weight. A subject specialist in Physics or Economics may be excellent at their subject and poor at this, because the skill is philosophical rather than technical. It is worth asking directly whether a tutor has taught TOK before agreeing to it.

mainEntity.name: We live in Bestech Park View Sanskruti. Which evening slots are realistically available?

acceptedAnswer.text: Slots between roughly four and six in the evening are easiest to fill locally, because a tutor can reach the Sector 48 to 50 belt before the worst of the Sohna Road traffic. Later slots exist but the pool is smaller and travel is unpredictable. Weekend mornings are usually the most reliable for a longer home session. Availability moves through the year as tutors fill their timetables, so a slot that was open in April may not be in September. Online timings are far more flexible.

mainEntity.name: Is Chemistry HL Paper 3 worth preparing separately?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, because it tests things the other papers do not. Paper 3 draws on experimental work and on the option content, and students who prepare only through general revision often meet unfamiliar question styles there for the first time in the exam hall. Practical technique, data analysis and the option topic all reward specific preparation. A useful check is to attempt one full past Paper 3 under timed conditions early, then decide how much separate attention it needs. Many students discover the gap is narrower than feared.

mainEntity.name: What should we expect to see after four weeks of tutoring?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not a grade change. Four weeks is too short for that in most subjects, and a tutor claiming otherwise is overselling. What should be visible is a written diagnostic from the first session, a record of topics covered, at least one piece of school-marked work the tutor has read and discussed, and a student who can explain what they are working on without prompting. Attitude usually shifts before marks do. If none of that is present, raise it rather than waiting for the next report.

mainEntity.name: Do you run group classes or a coaching centre near Sohna Road?

acceptedAnswer.text: Sessions arranged through IB Gram are one to one, at home or online, rather than centre-based batches. Group coaching works reasonably for a fixed board syllabus where everyone sits identical papers. It works poorly for the IB, where students in the same room may be on different subject levels, different internal assessment topics and different school deadlines. The value of individual sessions is that the plan follows one student's calendar. Small sibling or shared arrangements are occasionally possible and depend entirely on tutor agreement.

mainEntity.name: Our son does well in class but drops marks in exams. What changes that?

acceptedAnswer.text: Usually timing and command terms rather than knowledge. A student who understands a topic in a relaxed conversation can still lose marks by writing a description where the paper asked them to evaluate, or by spending eighteen minutes on a six-mark question. Work here looks unglamorous: timed sections, mark schemes read line by line, and rewriting answers to match what the command term requires. Improvement tends to appear in mocks rather than immediately. It also fades if timed practice stops, so it needs maintaining.

contentBlocks.heading: What the First IB Session Near Bestech Park View Spa, Gurugram Should Produce
contentBlocks.body:
A good opening session has a shape. The first ten minutes are the tutor asking questions and the student answering them, not the other way round. Then a few deliberately chosen tasks, pitched slightly above where the student is comfortable, because a task that is too easy tells nobody anything. Then a conversation about what went wrong in those tasks, done without flinching. And at the end, five minutes in which the tutor says out loud what they think the problem is.

Afterwards there should be something written. Half a page is enough: what the student can do unaided, the two or three places marks are leaking, and what the next few sessions will address.

contentBlocks.heading: Where a First Session Usually Lands: Math AI, Physics and English A
contentBlocks.body:
Different subjects reveal their problems in different ways during a diagnostic, and a tutor who knows the subject will go looking in the right place.

With Math AI HL, a good tutor will hand over a modelling question with a messy real-world context rather than a clean algebra exercise, because interpretation is usually where applications and interpretation students lose ground. Math AA HL students get tested on proof and algebraic manipulation instead. The two courses need genuinely different teaching instincts, and asking a candidate which they have taught more recently is a fair question.

Physics diagnostics tend to start with a graph or a data table rather than a formula, since uncertainty, units and interpretation account for a lot of quiet mark loss. Chemistry often starts with a written answer that reveals whether the student explains or merely asserts.

English A is unusual. A first session should involve the actual text the school has set, and a tutor who has not read it should say so plainly instead of teaching essay structure in the abstract. Economics sits between the two, mixing diagram accuracy with written evaluation.

contentBlocks.heading: What a Diagnostic Looks Like in PYP, MYP and the Diploma
contentBlocks.body:
A first session for a nine-year-old and a first session for a DP2 student have almost nothing in common beyond the name.

In the Primary Years Programme, covering ages 3 to 12, a diagnostic is mostly observation. Can the child read a question and restate it? Do they give up at the first difficulty or try something? A tutor who opens with a worksheet has already misread the programme.

In the Middle Years Programme, ages 11 to 16, the session should include one piece of the student's own marked work, because criterion-based feedback is where the useful information hides. A student who scored well on knowledge and badly on communication needs writing work, not more content.

In the Diploma Programme, ages 16 to 19, the diagnostic should touch the actual assessment. A past paper question under something close to exam timing, plus a look at whatever internal assessment work exists. For a DP1 student, the extended essay and theory of knowledge should at least be mentioned, since both are easier to plan early than to rescue late.

Support across all three runs from Grade 1 to Grade 12.

contentBlocks.heading: From First Enquiry to a Shortlist Worth Reading
contentBlocks.body:
The sequence is short enough to describe fully.

One, a call in which an advisor asks for the school, the programme year, the exact subject levels, the current marks and the practical constraints on timing. Two, a shortlist of two or three tutors, each described by what they have taught at that level and when they are genuinely free, rather than by adjectives. Three, a diagnostic session with one of them, treated as an assessment of the tutor as much as of the student. Four, a written note from that session. Five, your decision about whether a weekly arrangement follows.

The reason the shortlist stays small is that long lists transfer work back to the parent. Choosing between fifteen profiles is not a service.

One thing worth saying plainly: if you need a specific level at a specific hour and nobody strong is free then, an advisor should tell you that and suggest online instead of quietly offering a weaker match. Availability changes term by term and can be reviewed, but it cannot be invented on request.

contentBlocks.heading: The Part a First Session Cannot Tell You
contentBlocks.body:
A diagnostic is a good filter and a poor crystal ball. It shows you whether someone can explain, listen and diagnose. It cannot show you whether they will still be prepared in week nine, whether they will answer a message the night before a deadline, or whether they will keep pushing when the student stops finding it fun.

So the real checkpoints come later. By the third session there should be a visible plan and evidence that homework set is being checked rather than glanced at. By the eighth, the student should be able to attempt a question type that defeated them at the start, and you should have seen at least one piece of school-marked work discussed properly.

There are no guaranteed grades on offer here, no promised score jumps, no tutor numbers and no invented ratings, because none of that can be stood behind honestly.

An uncomfortable truth to add: a small number of students do not want tutoring at all and will treat every session as an imposition. Where that is the case, more hours make it worse, and a candid conversation is more valuable than a new tutor.

faqs.question: What exactly happens in the very first IB session?
faqs.answer: The tutor should spend the opening minutes asking questions rather than teaching, then set a few tasks chosen to find the edge of what the student can do alone. After that comes a discussion of what went wrong and why, and a spoken summary of the tutor's view. A short written note should follow, covering current strengths, where marks are being lost and a plan for the coming sessions. A session that consisted entirely of the tutor explaining is a warning sign, however impressive the explaining was.

faqs.question: Should a parent sit in on the first session?
faqs.answer: For a primary or lower middle years child, being nearby is sensible and often helps. For a teenager, sitting in usually changes the behaviour of everyone in the room, and the student performs for the parent instead of showing what they cannot do. A better approach with older students is to stay out and ask for the written note afterwards, then have a five-minute conversation with the tutor separately. The point is to see an honest picture, and an audience tends to prevent one.

faqs.question: Our son is in PYP Grade 4. Is a private tutor even appropriate at that age?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it depends entirely on what the concern is. If a child is behind on reading fluency or number confidence, focused short sessions help a great deal. If the concern is that the school reports feel vague and you want reassurance, a tutor is the wrong instrument and a conversation with the class teacher is the right one. At this age the risk is turning inquiry-based learning into drilling, which looks productive and undoes what the programme is trying to build.

faqs.question: How soon after we call can a tutor actually start?
faqs.answer: Online sessions can usually be set up faster, sometimes within a few days, because the tutor's travel is not a constraint. faqs.question: Can we ask for a different tutor if the first session feels flat?
faqs.answer: Yes, and doing it immediately is better than waiting. A flat first session is information. Say what specifically bothered you, since the detail is what makes the second match better: the tutor talked over him, she did not check the homework, he could not explain the marking criteria. A replacement is arranged where availability allows. faqs.question: How is Math AI HL different from Math AA HL, and does that change the tutor?
faqs.answer: It changes the tutor more than most families expect. Analysis and approaches leans on proof, calculus and algebraic manipulation. Applications and interpretation leans on modelling, statistics and reading meaning from a real context, and the exploration reflects that difference too. A tutor who has spent years on proof-heavy teaching can find modelling work oddly unfamiliar, and the reverse also happens. Schools generally prefer to know. Keeping the two sources of guidance aligned prevents a student receiving contradictory advice on the same draft.

faqs.answer: The advisory conversation and the shortlist are not charged for. What you pay for is teaching time, and rates depend on the programme year, the subject level and whether sessions are at home or online. Higher level Diploma subjects sit above primary support because the pool of tutors able to teach them well is smaller, and home sessions carry a premium reflecting travel. contentBlocks.heading: How IB Gram Builds a Tutor Shortlist for Central Park Flower Valley
contentBlocks.body:
The shortlist is built in five steps, and none of them begin with a tutor profile.

One, a short intake conversation: grade, programme, school, subject list, and what triggered the search. Two, the subject is broken down to the level that matters. Chemistry HL is not Chemistry SL, and a Math AA HL student stuck on proof by induction needs a different person from one who cannot finish Paper 2 inside the time. Three, we look at who has taught that exact combination and who is free in a slot you can realistically hold. Four, you receive two or three profiles rather than a directory, with teaching history and availability stated plainly. Five, the first session runs as a diagnostic, working through recent school assessments and past-paper responses to find where the marks are actually going.

A check-in follows around the fourth week. If the fit is wrong, say so then instead of at the end of a term. Tutor changes are ordinary and are not treated as a complaint.

Availability is the part nobody can promise in advance. A Physics HL specialist free at 6pm on Tuesdays may simply not exist in a given month, and we would rather say that than fill the slot with someone who has only ever taught a state board syllabus.

Subject split to HL or SL and to named weak areas

Four-week review built into the plan from the start

contentBlocks.heading: Subjects Parents Ask About Most on the Sohna Road Side of Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Six subjects account for most requests from this part of the city: Math AA HL, Math AI HL, Physics, Chemistry, Economics and English A.

The two mathematics routes are what families most often get wrong. Analysis and Approaches HL is proof-heavy and abstract, with calculus that runs well past school-level differentiation. Applications and Interpretation HL leans on modelling, statistics and confident use of the graphic display calculator. A student moved from AA HL to AI HL midway through Year 12 has to rebuild habits, not simply swap a textbook, and an IB maths tutor Central Park Flower Valley parents hire for one route will struggle with the other unless they have taught both.

Sciences bring a different bottleneck. Physics students lose marks on the option topic and on questions that ask them to explain rather than calculate. Chemistry internal assessments stall at the point where a student has data but no defensible uncertainty analysis. An IB science tutor Central Park Flower Valley families look for is usually being asked to repair one of those two things.

Economics HL adds a quantitative Paper 3 that rewards drill more than reading. English A Language and Literature needs Paper 1 practice on unseen texts, plus rehearsal for the individual oral, which students underprepare because it feels like a conversation rather than an examination.

Math AI HL: modelling, statistics, GDC technique
Physics: option topic and explanation-type questions
Chemistry: IA uncertainty and evaluation sections
Economics HL: Paper 3 quantitative drill
English A: unseen Paper 1 analysis and the individual oral

contentBlocks.heading: PYP, MYP and DP Support for Central Park Flower Valley Families
contentBlocks.body:
Support looks different at each stage, and the range covered runs from Grade 1 to Grade 12.

In the Primary Years Programme, ages three to twelve, the useful work is reading fluency, number sense and the ability to frame a question worth investigating. Turning that into worksheet drilling defeats the point of the programme. A good primary tutor resists the temptation even when a parent asks for more practice sheets, which parents often do.

The Middle Years Programme, ages eleven to sixteen, is where most families first feel lost. Marks arrive as criterion levels instead of percentages, and the personal project in the final year demands planning skills nobody has formally taught. Tutoring here is often half subject content and half translation: what is this criterion actually asking for.

The Diploma Programme, ages sixteen to nineteen, runs on deadlines. Internal assessments across six subjects, the extended essay, the TOK essay and exhibition, all landing in overlapping windows. For May 2026 candidates the pressure points are already visible. November 2026 candidates work to a different rhythm and often start too late. IB home tuition Central Park Flower Valley Gurugram families arrange during Year 11 tends to be calmer, and cheaper across two years, than a rescue attempt in February.

MYP: criteria A to D and personal project planning

May 2026 and November 2026 session planning
Grade 1 to Grade 12 covered

contentBlocks.heading: Tutor Checks Behind Every IB Shortlist in Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Screening is a filter, not a promise. This is what gets verified before a profile reaches a family in Central Park Flower Valley.

contentBlocks.heading: What Progress Should Look Like After Four Weeks
contentBlocks.body:
Four sessions in, evidence should be visible without asking the tutor for a summary.

The student should be able to say what a question is asking before attempting it. Command terms should have stopped being decoration on the page. An MYP student should be able to point at a criterion strand and name which part of the last assignment lost marks. A DP student should hold a research question for the internal assessment that survives a challenge, not a broad topic area. Timed past-paper attempts should exist on paper, marked, with errors sorted into categories rather than just crossed out.

What you should not expect inside four weeks is movement on the school report. Grades shift slowly, and anybody selling a faster number is selling something other than teaching.

If none of those signals appear, the honest step is to change tutors rather than extend the arrangement out of politeness. Ask for a different profile, keep the same subject brief, and lose one week instead of a term. Families who act early on a poor fit usually end up in a better position than families who wait for the next report card to confirm what they already suspected.

faqs.answer: You ask for a change, and you do it early. The four-week review exists partly for this. faqs.answer: It helps, though it is not essential. Campus familiarity mainly buys calendar awareness: when first IA drafts are due, how a department sequences option topics, how strict internal deadlines are. faqs.question: Does online tutoring genuinely work for internal assessments and the extended essay?
faqs.answer: For that kind of work it often works better than sitting in a room. IA and EE supervision is mostly reading drafts, marking against criteria and arguing about a research question. All of that travels well over a shared screen with an annotated document open, and the student watches comments appear as they are written. faqs.question: We are starting in Year 12 with mocks two months away. Is it too late?
faqs.answer: It is late, and it is worth being honest about what late means. Two months is enough to fix exam technique, cover one or two badly understood topics properly, and get timed past papers into a routine. It is not enough to rebuild two years of a subject learnt from a weak base. A tutor who promises otherwise is not being straight with you. The realistic plan is to pick the two highest-yield gaps, work those hard, then continue after the mocks.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does a Diploma Programme student actually need?
faqs.answer: For one subject, two sessions a week during term is a common pattern, dropping to one when things stabilise and rising in the weeks before mocks. Students taking help in three subjects at once are usually overloaded, and the fix is normally to repair the worst subject first rather than spread thinly. The interesting question is never which subject is hard. It is which paper is bleeding marks.

Chemistry students at higher level tend to be fine on Paper 1 and weak on the extended response sections of Paper 2, where an answer needs a mechanism explained rather than a value produced. Physics goes the other way for many students: the multiple choice paper punishes anyone slow at estimation, and the option topic gets taught late and revised last. An IB science tutor Central Park Resorts parents bring in during February is normally being asked to work on exactly those two habits, not to reteach the syllabus.

English A trouble usually shows up in the comparative paper, where students write two separate essays stapled together instead of one argument. Economics loses marks in evaluation, because students describe a diagram and stop before saying what follows from it.

Mathematics splits by route. Analysis and Approaches HL students struggle most with the problem-solving paper, which asks for sustained reasoning rather than recall. Applications and Interpretation HL students underuse their calculator and lose easy statistical marks. An IB maths tutor Central Park Resorts families hire should say which of the two routes they have actually taught, in which years.

Useful tutoring at this stage is diagnostic and gentle: reading level, number confidence, willingness to ask questions. Heavy drilling at seven years old buys a short-term number and costs the child later.

Middle Years Programme students, aged eleven to sixteen, hit two walls. The first is criterion-based marking, which rewards structure a student has never been shown. The second is the personal project, an independent piece of work with a long runway that most teenagers treat as a distant problem until it is not.

Diploma Programme students, sixteen to nineteen, live inside a calendar. Internal assessments, the extended essay, the TOK essay, and then a May 2026 or November 2026 sitting. November candidates get an extra half year and frequently waste it. Subject-choice regret also surfaces here, and a level change from HL to SL is worth discussing with the school early rather than in the final term.

contentBlocks.heading: Home Sessions Versus Online Sessions on the Sohna Road Corridor
contentBlocks.body:
Both formats work. They fail in different ways, which is the more useful thing to know.

Home tutoring fails on reliability. One tutor, one vehicle, one route through the Vatika Chowk and Subhash Chowk stretch at half past six in the evening. In good weeks that is a fifteen-minute inconvenience. Through the monsoon, or on a day when a road is dug up, it becomes a cancelled session, and cancelled sessions cluster in exactly the weeks before examinations. Against that, a person in the room is harder for a tired teenager to ignore, and written method errors get caught as they happen.

Online tutoring fails on attention and on anything physical. A Grade 4 child will drift. Laboratory technique cannot be taught over a call. What online buys is access to people who have actually marked at the level your child is sitting, plus late slots that no travelling tutor would accept, plus the option to record an explanation of a difficult derivation and watch it again on Sunday.

IB home tuition Central Park Resorts Gurugram families often start with is a weekday evening pattern. What they end the year with is usually a mix.

Online sessions break down on attention with younger children
Late evening slots are far easier to fill online

Practical laboratory technique needs a room, not a screen

contentBlocks.heading: From First Call to First Session for a Central Park Resorts Family
contentBlocks.body:
Counted in days rather than steps, the sequence usually looks like this.

Day zero is a conversation, fifteen minutes at most. We want the grade, the programme, the school, the subject with its level, the specific thing that has gone wrong, and the two or three weekly slots that survive contact with school timings, sport and travel. Guessing at any of that costs a fortnight later.

Days one to three are matching. Tutors are filtered by programme experience first, then by subject level, then by whether they can hold your slot without a heroic commute. You get two or three profiles with teaching history and availability written plainly, not a searchable list of hundreds.

Day four or five is the diagnostic session. The tutor works through your child's own marked scripts and a short piece of past-paper work rather than delivering a prepared first lesson. You should receive a short written read on what is wrong and what the first month will target.

Week four is the review. Keep it in the calendar even if things are going well, because that is the meeting where a small drift gets corrected cheaply. Availability throughout depends on tutor schedules and is confirmed, never assumed.

contentBlocks.heading: The Screening a Tutor Passes Before a Profile Reaches You
contentBlocks.body:
It is easier to describe screening by what it rejects.

Anyone who opens with a promised grade is removed. Nobody can guarantee a 7, a points total or a percentage gain, and a tutor willing to say otherwise in a first conversation will say worse things to a nervous sixteen-year-old. Anyone claiming Diploma Programme experience who cannot describe how an internal assessment is marked is removed. Anyone unwilling to sit a short subject task at the level they want to teach is removed, because that refusal is the single most reliable signal in the whole process.

What is positively checked: government photo identification, degree and teaching qualification documents rather than a stated claim, teaching history for the specific programme, and references from earlier families where those exist. The subject task is marked by someone who knows the criteria, so a technically correct answer written in the wrong register still gets flagged.

The limitation is worth stating plainly. Screening improves the odds of a good match. It cannot predict chemistry between a particular tutor and a particular teenager, and it does not replace your own judgement after watching two sessions and reading the work that comes back.

contentBlocks.heading: What Tutoring Cannot Fix, and What It Reliably Can
contentBlocks.body:
Start with the honest limits, because they save money.

Tutoring cannot rebuild two years of missed foundations in six weeks. It cannot make a student who refuses to attempt work between sessions improve, since the session itself is a small share of the week. It cannot repair an internal assessment begun three days before the deadline, and it cannot raise a predicted grade by decree.

What it does reliably is narrower and still worth paying for. Exam technique improves quickly, often within a month, because most lost marks come from misreading command terms and mismanaging time rather than from ignorance. Written work improves when someone marks it against the actual criteria and hands it back with the strand that failed named. Confidence improves when a student stops discovering their weaknesses for the first time in an examination hall.

By the fourth week you should be able to see specific things: marked timed papers with errors grouped by type, a research question that has survived a challenge, and a child who can say what a question is asking before starting it. If those are absent, change the tutor rather than adding hours. Adding hours to a bad match only makes the bill larger.

faqs.question: Is it worth starting a tutor eight weeks before the May session?
faqs.answer: Yes, provided the goal is narrowed. Eight weeks is enough to fix timing, rehearse command terms, and drill past papers under exam conditions in one or two subjects. It is not enough to cover a syllabus that was never learnt. Families who spread eight weeks across four subjects usually see very little from any of them. Pick the subject where technique rather than knowledge is costing marks, put the hours there, and treat the rest as revision the student manages alone.

faqs.question: Can sessions run after 8pm, given how late school buses get back?
faqs.answer: Late slots exist, and they are much easier to fill online than at home. A tutor willing to travel to Sector 48 and start at half past eight is rare, and one who agrees in a first call often cannot sustain it past a month. Online tutors can. If your child is genuinely unavailable before eight because of bus timings or sport, plan for an online arrangement from the start rather than trying home sessions first and rebooking in week three.

faqs.question: Do you cover retakes for the November session?
faqs.answer: Retake support is arranged the same way as a first sitting, with one difference: the diagnostic matters more. A student retaking a subject already has a real examination script and a component-level result, which shows precisely which paper failed. That is far better information than a school report. Planning usually works backwards from November, with heavier work in the middle months and technique rehearsal near the end. Availability of a specialist in a given subject depends on tutor schedules and is confirmed before anything is booked.

faqs.question: How do you handle two children in the same house at different IB stages?
faqs.answer: They are treated as two separate matches, because a good MYP mathematics teacher and a Diploma Programme Physics specialist are almost never the same person. Some families try to save time with one tutor covering both and it usually disappoints the older child. Scheduling can still be shared sensibly, with back-to-back slots on the same evening so the house has one disrupted night rather than two. Fees for each match are quoted separately and agreed before either arrangement starts.

faqs.question: We live here but our child studies at a school on Golf Course Road. Does that matter?
faqs.answer: It matters for timing more than for teaching. A longer bus route pushes the earliest workable session to around quarter past six, which shrinks the pool of tutors who can travel and still reach home at a reasonable hour. It also means the school's internal deadlines, not your locality, set the work rhythm. Bring the assessment calendar to the intake call. The tutor plans backwards from those dates, and IB Gram holds no affiliation with the school itself.

faqs.question: Are group sessions available, or is it one to one only?
faqs.answer: Most arrangements are one to one, because IB work is diagnostic and two students rarely lose marks in the same place. Small groups can make sense in narrow situations: two friends in the same class, same level, sitting the same session, revising a shared topic before mocks. Beyond that the format dilutes quickly. If cost is the reason for asking, a shorter one-to-one session every week is usually better value than a longer group one, and easier to keep consistent.

faqs.question: What happens if a tutor keeps cancelling sessions?
faqs.answer: Tell us early rather than absorbing it. Repeated cancellation is the most common reason a home arrangement quietly stops working, and it clusters in monsoon months and in the weeks before examinations, which is exactly when a student can least afford it. The usual fix is either to move that tutor's sessions online, which removes the travel that caused the problem, or to replace the match entirely. Both are handled without cost to the family beyond the sessions already delivered.

faqs.question: For Chemistry HL, is a serving school teacher better than a full-time tutor?
faqs.answer: Each brings something different. A serving teacher knows current marking behaviour and departmental expectations well. A full-time tutor usually has more experience diagnosing individual students, more availability, and more patience for the slow repetition a weak topic needs. The decision should rest on the specific problem. Internal assessment guidance often suits someone with recent marking experience. Rebuilding organic chemistry from a shaky base often suits whoever can give consistent weekly time. Availability of either depends on tutor schedules.

Yes, a tutor can come to your home, and for most subjects there will be more than one candidate. That is the honest answer, and it is different from the answer families get in the newer sectors further south.

contentBlocks.heading: Which IB Programme Your Child Is In Changes What You Should Ask For
contentBlocks.body:
Ask for the wrong thing and even a strong tutor underdelivers. The right request differs by stage across Grade 1 to Grade 12.

For a Primary Years Programme child, aged three to twelve, the useful request is a reading and number assessment, followed by a plan you can understand without jargon. Do not ask for extra worksheets. Ask what the child can do independently and what they still need prompting for. That single distinction predicts the next two years better than any score.

For a Middle Years Programme student, eleven to sixteen, the request should name a criterion. Not help with Science, but help with criterion C on the last investigation, where the analysis was thin. Teachers write those comments on returned work and parents rarely read them. The personal project deserves a separate conversation, ideally six months before it is due rather than six weeks.

For a Diploma Programme student, sixteen to nineteen, the request should name a component: an internal assessment, the extended essay, the TOK essay, or a specific paper. May 2026 and November 2026 candidates are working to different clocks, and a November candidate who starts in the same month as a May candidate has effectively started late.

MYP: name the criterion that lost marks
DP: name the component, whether IA, EE, TOK or a paper
Personal project talks belong six months out
May and November candidates run on different clocks

DLF Phase 1, DLF Phase 4 and DLF Phase 5 are effectively next door. Sushant Lok and the Sector 53 and Sector 54 stretch along the Rapid Metro corridor are minutes away in clear conditions. Sector 57 and Sector 65 are short runs. South City 1, Sector 50 and Nirvana Country are reasonable, and Sohna Road communities such as Orchid Petals and the Southern Peripheral Road side are longer but not unusual.

The caveat is that Golf Course Road itself is one of the slowest stretches in the city between six and eight in the evening. A tutor coming three kilometres along it at seven can take longer than a tutor covering nine kilometres on a clearer route. Distance on a map and distance in minutes stop agreeing at exactly the hour you want a session.

Practical consequence: fix a slot and keep it. A tutor who has planned their evening around a Tuesday at 6.30 will hold it. A family that moves the time each week gradually loses the tutor to someone who does not.

Students need a topic with real mathematics in it, at their own level, that can be developed over a substantial written piece with genuine personal engagement. Choosing badly costs weeks, and a good IB maths tutor DLF Beverly Park families work with will spend the first session on the topic rather than on the writing.

Economics requires commentaries drawn from recent news articles across different sections of the syllabus, which means students must start collecting material early or find themselves hunting for a suitable article in the final week. Chemistry and Physics investigations run on a limited number of practical hours, so a poorly framed research question wastes laboratory time that cannot be recovered. An IB science tutor DLF Beverly Park parents bring in for coursework should be reading a draft, not delivering a lecture.

contentBlocks.heading: The Matching Sequence, Told Plainly
contentBlocks.body:
Four questions, then a shortlist, then a diagnostic. That is the whole process.

The four questions are: which programme and grade, which subject and at what level, what specifically has gone wrong, and which two or three weekly slots will survive a normal school term. The last one is answered carelessly more often than the others, and it is the one that decides whether an arrangement lasts past a month.

The shortlist is two or three profiles, not a browsable list. Each carries teaching history for the programme in question, the levels taught, and honest availability. If nobody suitable is free in your slot, you are told that rather than offered a near miss. A tutor who has taught the subject only at standard level is not presented for higher level work, even when they are free and pleasant and nearby.

The diagnostic session comes next. The tutor reads your child's recent marked work, sets a short timed task, and reports back on where marks are being lost. Only then does a plan get written. Booking a term of sessions before that step is the most common way families waste money, and it is easy to avoid.

Two or three profiles with levels and availability stated

Diagnostic session before any teaching plan

contentBlocks.heading: When a DLF Beverly Park Family Should Pick Online Over Home Sessions
contentBlocks.body:
Home is the sensible default from this address. There are three situations where it is the wrong call.

The first is a rare higher level combination. If your child needs Math AI HL, a particular Physics option topic, or a less common language B, the number of people in the city who have genuinely taught it is small, and insisting on a travelling tutor narrows an already narrow pool. An IB online tutor DLF Beverly Park parents engage in those cases is often considerably stronger than the local alternative.

The second is timing. If sport, music or a long bus route pushes the only free slot past eight in the evening, a travelling tutor will agree once and resent it by week four. Online works cleanly at that hour.

The third is exam season. In the six weeks before a session, short frequent contact beats long weekly meetings, and nobody can travel four times a week. Families often keep the same tutor and simply move the arrangement online for that stretch.

Outside those three, take the person who comes to the house. A teenager with a laptop open and no adult in the room is not concentrating as hard as you think.

contentBlocks.heading: Judging a Tutor Before the Report Card Does
contentBlocks.body:
You do not have to wait a term to know whether this is working. Three checks, none of which require you to understand the subject.

Sit in on ten minutes of the second or third session. You are listening for questions being asked of the student rather than explanation being delivered at them. A tutor talking for eight of those ten minutes is teaching to their own comfort, not to the child's gaps.

Read one piece of marked work. Comments should name what to change and where, in the language of the assessment criteria. A tick and a number tell you nothing. If you cannot tell from the marking what the student should do differently next time, neither can the student.

Ask your child one question after a fortnight: what is this tutor working on with you. A clear answer, naming a topic or a skill, is a good sign. A vague answer about doing questions means there is no plan.

What you should not use as a check is the school report, because it lags by weeks and mixes in a dozen other variables. And nobody should be promising you a grade in exchange for hours.

Ask the student what the tutor is working on

Treat any promised grade as a warning

contentBlocks.heading: Checks Run on Tutors Working in Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Before a profile is shared, a tutor supplies documents rather than descriptions.

Government photo identification is verified. Degree certificates and teaching qualifications are checked as documents, not accepted as claims on a profile. Teaching history is examined for the specific programme, since experience with one curriculum does not transfer automatically to internal assessment supervision under another. A short subject task at the level the tutor wants to teach is set and marked by someone who knows the criteria. References from earlier families are contacted where they exist.

There are things this site deliberately does not publish. No tutor counts, because a large number tells a parent nothing about the one person who will sit with their child. No star ratings, no invented success percentages, and no testimonials that cannot be traced to a real family.

The limitation is straightforward. Verification establishes that a tutor is who they say and knows what they claim. It cannot establish that this particular adult will work well with your particular teenager. That question is answered in the first two sessions, which is why the four-week review exists and why changing a tutor is treated as routine rather than as a complaint.

Start with a short call. Fifteen minutes is enough if the basics are ready.

Bring the subject list with levels, the last piece of marked work, the exam session your child is sitting, and the evening slots that will still be free in March. faqs.question: Do enough IB tutors travel to DLF Beverly Park for home sessions?
faqs.answer: For most subjects, yes. faqs.question: How long should a single session be?
faqs.answer: Sixty to ninety minutes suits most students. Younger children in the Primary Years Programme do better with forty-five, because attention rather than time is the limiting factor. Two-hour sessions after a full school day look efficient on a calendar and rarely are, since the last half hour usually gets very little done. For coursework work such as an exploration or an extended essay, shorter and more frequent contact beats long sittings, because drafts need time between meetings to actually be written.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the extended essay if their subject is different?
faqs.answer: Only partly, and it is worth being clear about the split. Structure, research question framing, argument discipline and referencing are general skills that a capable tutor from a neighbouring subject can support well. Subject-specific judgement, such as whether a chemistry investigation is viable or whether an economics argument holds, needs someone from that subject. The school supervisor remains the formal guide in every case, and no tutor should be positioning themselves as a replacement for that relationship.

faqs.question: My son is in MYP and the school says he is fine. Should we still arrange support?
faqs.answer: Often the honest answer is no. If criterion levels are steady and returned work carries comments he understands and acts on, adding a tutor mainly adds hours. The case for starting early is different: a student heading into Diploma Programme sciences or higher level mathematics with shaky algebra benefits from quiet foundation work now rather than emergency work in Year 12. Ask the school which specific skills would matter most later, then decide with that answer rather than with a general worry.

faqs.question: What should I look for in the first ten minutes of a session I sit in on?
faqs.answer: Listen to the balance of talk. A tutor who explains for eight straight minutes is teaching at your child rather than diagnosing them. Good sessions open with a question about the last piece of work, then a problem the student attempts while the tutor watches. You also want to hear the vocabulary of the assessment used naturally, criterion names or command terms, because those are what marks are awarded against. Silence while a student thinks is a good sign, not an awkward one.

faqs.question: Are fees higher on Golf Course Road than elsewhere in Gurugram?
faqs.answer: Rates are set by subject, level and format rather than by postcode. What does change locally is the travel component. Golf Course Road slows badly between six and eight in the evening, so a tutor accepting a home slot here is committing more time than the session length suggests, and that shows up in the quoted figure. Taking the same tutor online usually removes the difference. Every figure is agreed during the intake conversation, before a first session is arranged.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram have any tie-up with DLF Beverly Park or with the developer?
faqs.answer: No. There is no arrangement with the society, its management, its residents body or the developer, no permission to operate on the premises, and no endorsement of any kind. IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and families here contact it directly, exactly as families elsewhere in the city do. faqs.question: Can we pause during school holidays and resume afterwards?
faqs.answer: Pausing is normal, particularly over long summer breaks and family travel. Two things are worth knowing. A tutor who holds a fixed weekday slot may not be able to keep it open indefinitely, so a long pause sometimes means a different time on return or a different tutor. And Diploma Programme students in the summer between Year 11 and Year 12 often get more value from a light schedule than from a complete stop, since that period is when extended essay work can be done calmly.

faqs.question: What information should I not have to ask for?
faqs.answer: You should be told, without prompting, which levels the tutor has actually taught and for how long, what the diagnostic session found, what the first month will target, and how availability might change during exam season. You should also be told plainly when nobody suitable is free, rather than being offered someone close enough. If any of that has to be extracted from the platform or the tutor, treat it as information about how the rest of the arrangement will go.

contentBlocks.heading: Study Habits Come First, Then the IB Tutor: DLF Carlton Estate, Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Most parents near DLF Carlton Estate do not begin by searching for a tutor. They begin by noticing something small. A Grade 9 student who reads a question twice and still answers a different question. A DP student who finishes past papers but never marks them against the actual rubric. A ten-year-old who can explain a science idea out loud and freezes the moment it has to go on paper.

Those are habits, not gaps in knowledge. And habits are the first thing a competent IB tutor changes, usually within three or four sessions, long before any topic is retaught.

So the sensible way to read this page is backwards from the habit you have already noticed. If the problem is command terms, you want someone who marks work the way an examiner does. If the problem is that homework expands to fill the whole evening, you want someone who will impose a timetable and then hold the student to it. If the problem is one unit in Chemistry, six focused sessions may be enough, and a year-long arrangement would be a waste.

IB tutors in DLF Carlton Estate Gurugram are usually approached at one of three moments: a report that slips a band, an internal assessment draft that comes back heavily annotated, or a mock result a few months before the May session. Each of those calls for a different kind of person, and the difference is worth naming out loud before you start.

contentBlocks.heading: Where a Tutor Can Realistically Reach DLF Carlton Estate in Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
DLF Carlton Estate sits inside the DLF Phase 5 belt along Golf Course Road, with The Crest, DLF Park Place and DLF The Pinnacle in the immediate neighbourhood and the Sector 53 and Sector 54 stretch of the Rapid Metro corridor a short drive away. That position decides one very practical thing: who can teach your child at 6 pm on a Tuesday.

A tutor already teaching in DLF Phase 4, South City 1 or Sushant Lok can usually chain a second session near Golf Course Road without much difficulty. A tutor coming from Vatika Chowk on Sohna Road, or out past Sector 65 on Golf Course Extension Road, is a different proposition on a school night. The distance on a map is modest. The distance at 6:30 pm is not, and a tutor who arrives frayed after forty minutes of traffic teaches worse than one who logs in from home.

Home tutoring may be available across the DLF phases, Sushant Lok, Sector 57, Nirvana Country and the Sohna Road side, subject to tutor availability and the day requested. Rather than promising coverage, the honest version is this: ask for a home slot, and if nobody credible is free at your hour, take the online option for that subject instead of accepting a weaker match who happens to live close by.

Short hop: Sector 53, Sector 54, Rapid Metro corridor, DLF Phase 4

contentBlocks.heading: Home, Online or a Mix: Choosing a Mode for Carlton Estate Evenings
contentBlocks.body:
The mode decision is usually made badly, because parents treat home tutoring as the premium option and online as the fallback. For IB, in certain subjects, it is closer to the opposite.

Home sessions earn their value with younger students. A PYP or early MYP child benefits from someone sitting beside them, watching how they set out a page, catching the exact moment attention drifts. Screens are weaker at that.

For DP subjects the calculation flips. Math AA HL, Physics HL and Economics HL need someone who has taught that specific level and marked work at it. The pool of such tutors within a fifteen-minute drive of Golf Course Road is small, and narrowing it further by insisting on home visits often means trading subject depth for convenience. Online lessons open the pool to specialists anywhere in Delhi or Noida, with a shared whiteboard, annotated past papers, and recordings a student can replay the night before a test.

A hybrid pattern works for many families around DLF Carlton Estate: one home session a week so accountability stays visible, one online session for the technical heavy lifting. Say plainly which subjects you want in which mode when you first speak to an advisor. It changes the shortlist considerably, and it saves a round of introductions that were never going to work.
items: Home sessions: strongest for PYP, MYP and students who need supervision
Online: widest choice of HL specialists, replayable recordings
Hybrid: accountability at home, depth on screen
Late evening or rare subject requests usually resolve faster online

contentBlocks.heading: Subject by Subject: What IB Tuition Near DLF Carlton Estate Covers in Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Math is the most requested subject and the most frequently mismatched. Math AA and Math AI are not interchangeable, and a tutor comfortable with AI SL statistics may struggle with AA HL proof or the calculus option. Ask which of the two a tutor has taught most recently, at which level, and what they do differently for the calculator paper against the non-calculator paper.

Physics and Chemistry requests usually arrive with a specific unit attached rather than a general complaint: thermodynamics, organic mechanisms, circular motion. That is good news. A targeted block of sessions on one unit plus its data-based questions is cheaper and faster than an open-ended arrangement, and easier to judge.

Economics support tends to be about writing rather than content. Students know the diagrams and lose marks on evaluation, on real-world examples, on the gap between explain and discuss.

English A splits into two quite different needs: Paper 1 unseen analysis, and the individual oral with its global issue. A tutor who is excellent at the first is not automatically useful for the second, so ask about both.

Across all of these, an IB science tutor near DLF Carlton Estate should be able to show you the assessment criteria they are teaching against before the first session ends.

Math AI HL and SL: modelling, statistics, graphic calculator fluency
Physics and Chemistry: unit-level blocks, data questions, lab write-ups
Economics: evaluation language and real-world examples
English A: Paper 1 unseen work and individual oral preparation

contentBlocks.heading: How a Shortlist Gets Built for a Family in DLF Phase 5
contentBlocks.body:
The process is deliberately unglamorous, and it runs in four steps.

One: a short conversation about the student rather than the subject. Current grade, school, which programme, what the last two pieces of assessed work looked like, and what the evening actually contains once activities and travel are counted honestly.

Two: a filter on level and assessment experience. A request for DP Chemistry HL with an internal assessment due in six weeks is a different search from Grade 6 MYP science. The first needs someone who has supervised IA methodology and error analysis. The second needs someone patient with concept-based tasks and unhurried explanation.

Three: a filter on logistics. Which days, which hour, home or online, and whether a family near DLF Carlton Estate can hold that slot for a full term. A brilliant tutor available only on Thursdays at 9 pm is no match for a Grade 5 student.

Four: a shortlist with reasons attached, so you can see why each name is on it. You speak to them. You choose.

If nobody on that shortlist convinces you, say so and ask for a second round. That is a normal outcome rather than a failure, and it costs far less than six weeks spent with the wrong person.

contentBlocks.heading: PYP, MYP and DP: The Habit That Changes at Each Stage
contentBlocks.body:
Each IB stage asks for a different working habit, and most tutoring goes wrong when the tutor brings the wrong one.

In the Primary Years Programme, ages three to twelve, the habit is curiosity that survives contact with a worksheet. Support here means reading fluency, number sense and the confidence to ask a question in class. It should not mean drilling a seven-year-old through pages of sums because that is what tuition looked like a generation ago.

In the Middle Years Programme, ages eleven to sixteen, the habit is translation. Students understand a concept and then have to express it against criteria A to D, with command terms doing real work in the wording. Marks disappear in that translation far more often than in the understanding itself. MYP support that never mentions the criteria is not MYP support.

In the Diploma Programme, ages sixteen to nineteen, the habit is planning. Six subjects, internal assessments, the Extended Essay, TOK, CAS, and mocks stacked against school deadlines. A DP tutor working with a student near DLF Carlton Estate should spend part of the first month on a calendar and not only on content, because the students who struggle in the second year are rarely the ones who did not know the material.

DP: IA planning, EE supervision support, TOK essay structure

contentBlocks.heading: What Gets Checked Before an IB Tutor Is Put in Front of Your Child
contentBlocks.body:
Screening is a set of questions, not a badge. Before a tutor reaches a shortlist, the checks cover identity and contactability, claimed qualifications, the subjects and levels they say they have taught, and how recently they have taught them. A tutor who last taught DP Physics in 2016 is a different proposition from one teaching it this term, and both may be entirely honest.

The part that matters most is teaching evidence. A tutor is asked to describe how they would open with a student scoring in the middle band, what work they would want to see first, and how they would mark a sample answer. Vague replies are informative.

What screening cannot do is predict chemistry between a particular tutor and a particular teenager. So the first two sessions should be treated as a trial by both sides, and changing tutor early is not a setback.

Parents near DLF Carlton Estate should run their own short check too. Ask which level the tutor has actually taught. Ask what the student will be doing in the first ten minutes of a session. Ask what evidence of progress you should expect to see in four weeks, and write the answer down.

contentBlocks.heading: Honest Limits of What a Tutoring Platform Can Promise
contentBlocks.body:
No tutoring arrangement can promise a grade. Anyone who does is either guessing or selling. What can be described is the process, and what you should be able to see after a month of consistent sessions.

By week four, three things should be visible: a written plan naming the units and assessments being targeted, marked work carrying comments tied to criteria rather than ticks, and a student who can tell you what they are working on without checking their phone. If none of that exists after four weeks, the arrangement is not working, and saying so early is the kinder option for everyone.

There are honest limits on availability as well. Home tutoring near DLF Carlton Estate depends on which tutors are free on the exact day and hour you want, and the slots between 6 pm and 8 pm fill first. A request for a rare higher level subject at short notice before the May session may only be answerable online.

Starting late narrows what is achievable. A student who begins DP support eight weeks before final papers can sharpen exam technique and recover specific topics. Rebuilding two years of foundations in that window is not realistic, and pretending otherwise wastes a family's money.

contentBlocks.heading: Starting the Conversation From DLF Carlton Estate, Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
The first message does not need to be long. It needs four things: the child's grade and programme, the subjects and levels in question, two or three time windows that genuinely work on a school night, and one sentence about the habit you have noticed at home.

With that, an advisor can check which IB tutors in DLF Carlton Estate Gurugram may be free for home sessions and which subjects would be better served online. You get a small shortlist rather than a long one, with a note on why each name is there.

Then a first session. Expect it to be mostly diagnostic: a look at recent marked work, a few questions pitched slightly above current level, and a short plan agreed out loud with the student in the room. Content teaching usually begins properly in session two, once the tutor knows what is genuinely missing rather than what was reported as missing.

If you are unsure whether to start now or after the next round of school assessments, ask that question directly. Waiting two weeks and starting with real marked work in hand sometimes produces a better first month than starting tomorrow with nothing to look at.

introSummary: IB tutors in DLF Crest Gurugram can be arranged for home sessions across the Golf Course Road belt or online across the city, from Grade 1 to Grade 12 in PYP, MYP and the Diploma Programme. Online wins on two counts: access to a tutor who has taught your exact subject at your exact level, and past-paper work where the question, the markscheme and the script share one screen. It loses with younger children and students who need someone present to begin. Both modes cover IA, EE, TOK and revision for the May 2026 and November 2026 sessions.

contentBlocks.heading: What online IB tutoring does better for DLF Crest families in Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Online tutoring is usually offered as the convenient option. That undersells it in one direction and oversells it in another.

What it genuinely does better is reach. A student here needing Math AI HL statistics support, or an economics tutor who has actually marked HL evaluation, is choosing from tutors across the whole city instead of the ones willing to drive to Golf Course Road at eight in the evening. Screen sharing also suits past-paper work better than a dining table does, because the question, the markscheme and the student own script can sit open together and be annotated live. Sessions start on time regardless of what the Golf Course Road stretch is doing.

Where it does not: a nine-year-old on a screen drifts, and no amount of good teaching fixes that inside a fifty-minute slot. Students who need a person present to begin work do worse online. Anything involving equipment, handwriting speed under exam conditions, or a parent within earshot works better in person.

Support runs Grade 1 to Grade 12 across PYP, MYP and the Diploma Programme, with both modes available and both worth judging against the specific child.

Screen sharing beats a dining table for past papers
Start times unaffected by Golf Course Road traffic
Younger children drift on screens
In person for handwriting speed and equipment work

contentBlocks.heading: How a DLF Crest request is matched, step by step
contentBlocks.body:
The process is short, and each step exists to remove a specific failure.

The enquiry carries programme, year, subject, level, whatever the school has said, and the times that work. An advisor calls, because written enquiries under-describe the problem about as often as they describe it accurately. A parent asking for Chemistry help may need internal assessment structure. A parent asking for exam strategy may have a child who has stopped opening the textbook.

The shortlist is built against the call, not the form. Level comes first, then assessment stage, then timing, then mode. Availability is checked when the shortlist is prepared rather than assumed in advance, because tutor schedules shift between terms.

You then talk to the tutor, or run one session, before committing to anything. If the fit is wrong, say so and the list is revisited. That is expected rather than awkward.

Two honest caveats. A rare combination, an HL subject at a late evening hour for instance, can take several days to fill. And a fast match that ignores level is worse than a slower one that respects it, which is why the call is not skipped.

contentBlocks.heading: PYP, MYP and DP: where the screen helps and where it does not
contentBlocks.body:
The three programmes respond to online teaching very differently, which is worth knowing before a mode is chosen.

Primary Years, ages three to twelve, is the hardest to run on a screen. Inquiry-led learning depends on a child talking, wandering off the point and being brought back, and that is difficult through a laptop. Where online does work at this stage is short, frequent reading or number-sense sessions with a parent nearby, not hour-long lessons.

Middle Years, ages eleven to sixteen, sits in between. Criterion-related assessment means a good deal of the work is written, and reviewing a marked task against the descriptor works perfectly well on a shared screen. Planning a practical investigation is better in person.

Diploma, ages sixteen to nineteen, is where online tends to win outright. Internal assessment drafting, extended essay scoping, theory of knowledge argument and past-paper technique are all document-and-discussion work. A DP2 student can take a session at nine at night after finishing an assignment, which a travelling tutor simply cannot offer.

Concept-based teaching and command-term language matter in all three, whichever mode you settle on.

MYP: written criterion work reviews well on screen
MYP practicals: better in person
DP: IA, EE, TOK and past papers suit the screen

contentBlocks.heading: Home sessions at DLF Crest, Gurugram, and the case for each mode
contentBlocks.body:
Home tutoring may be available across Golf Course Road, the DLF phases, Sushant Lok, Sector 57, Sohna Road and nearby communities depending on tutor schedules, and this address sits close to the middle of that band. It is one of the easier places in Gurugram to fill a home slot, which is why the case for online here has to be made on quality rather than convenience.

Make it on quality where the subject is narrow. A tutor who has supervised Math AA HL internal assessments repeatedly is worth more than a competent generalist who happens to live fifteen minutes away.

Make the case for home visits where attention is the problem. If your child needs someone at the table to begin, a screen will not solve it, and the honest advice is to accept the smaller pool of local tutors and work with it.

Hybrid is common along this stretch: one home session a week for accountability, one or two online sessions for drilling and doubt-solving before a test. Visitor entry at the tower gate is worth arranging for the term rather than each visit.

Whichever mode you pick, keep the session time fixed. Moveable slots are the most common reason a term drifts.

contentBlocks.heading: Subject-level requests from DLF Crest and Golf Course Road
contentBlocks.body:
Math AA HL, Math AI HL, Physics, Chemistry, Economics and English A cover most of what is asked for here. A better filter than the subject name is what you ask the tutor to demonstrate in the first conversation.

For Math AA HL, ask them to talk through a proof question and say what students typically lose marks for. For Math AI HL, ask how they teach a student to write the interpretation paragraph that follows a correct model.

For Physics or Chemistry, ask what makes an internal assessment research question too broad, and how they handle uncertainty and error discussion, which is where marks quietly disappear.

For Economics, ask them to distinguish an eight-mark explanation from a fifteen-mark evaluation. For English A, ask how they build unseen commentary skill across a term rather than a fortnight, because Paper 1 does not respond to last-minute effort.

An answer that stays general is itself the answer. Subject knowledge is common. Assessment knowledge at a specific level is not, and that is the thing you are actually buying.

Bring the last marked script to that conversation. It moves the discussion from opinion to evidence in about two minutes.

contentBlocks.heading: Reading the first month honestly
contentBlocks.body:
The first month is a test of the arrangement, not of the child.

Three questions are worth asking at week four. Does the student now bring specific questions to the session rather than a general sense of being stuck? Has the tutor described a weakness you did not already know about? And has anything in the daily routine changed, homework started earlier, fewer arguments about it, one subject no longer the dreaded one?

Marks are the last thing to move, and sometimes they dip first. A student who begins attempting the harder parts of a paper instead of skipping them will lose marks in the short term and gain them later. Read the attempt rate, not only the score.

Nobody can promise an outcome. Guaranteed grades, promised sevens and percentage improvement figures are not things a tutor can honestly offer, and being offered one is a reason to ask harder questions rather than relax.

What can be committed to is a plan, regular session notes, and a straight answer when progress stalls. If week four shows nothing at all, change the tutor rather than adding hours.

contentBlocks.heading: Vetting that matters more when the tutor is on a screen
contentBlocks.body:
Vetting matters in both modes, and slightly differently online.

The common checks: photo identity, the qualification claimed, and teaching history at the specific level rather than in the subject generally. Having taught chemistry for years is not evidence of having taught Chemistry HL against IB criteria, and the difference shows up around week three. Reliability is checked too, punctuality and cancellations, since a tutor who moves sessions weekly costs you more than the fee.

Online adds two things worth confirming yourself. The first is that the person teaching is the person you interviewed, which is why cameras stay on and why a first session should feel continuous with the introductory call. The second is the setup: a stable connection, a way to annotate a document or write on a shared board, and the habit of sending notes or the annotated script afterwards. A tutor who only talks at a camera for an hour is running a phone call.

For home sessions here, ask for identification at the gate on the first visit. It is a reasonable request and a serious tutor will expect it.

Decide the mode question before you send anything, because it changes the shortlist. If the need is a narrow higher level specialism or a late slot, say online. If the need is attention and accountability, say home, and accept a smaller pool. If you are unsure, ask for both and take a first session in each.

faqs.question: Is online really as effective as a tutor in the room for DP subjects?
faqs.answer: For Diploma work, generally yes, and sometimes better. Internal assessment drafting, extended essay scoping and past-paper technique are document-and-discussion tasks, and a shared screen holds the question, the markscheme and the student script side by side in a way a dining table cannot. The gap appears elsewhere: practical set-up, handwriting speed under timed conditions, and students who need physical presence to start working. If your DP student already works independently, online usually buys the better tutor rather than the nearer one.

faqs.question: Our building requires visitor pre-approval. Does that complicate home tuition?
faqs.answer: It adds a step, not a problem. Ask whether your tower allows a tutor to be registered for the term rather than approved on each visit, since a fifteen-minute wait at the gate takes a real bite out of an hour. Share the gate and parking details with the tutor before the first session. On that first visit it is reasonable to ask to see the identification the platform verified. After that the routine settles and entry stops being a topic at all.

faqs.question: Which is better value, home or online?
faqs.answer: Value depends on what is scarce for you. Online removes travel from the fee structure and widens the choice of tutor, so for a narrow higher level subject it usually buys more expertise per rupee. A home visit carries travel time, which is reflected in the rate, and buys presence and accountability that some students genuinely need. The expensive option is neither of those: it is paying for months of sessions with a tutor who does not know the assessment at your child level.

faqs.question: My child is in MYP4 and the school report is fine, but she says she is lost. Who is right?
faqs.answer: Both, usually. A report reflects classwork, participation and completed tasks. Feeling lost is often about the gap between following a lesson and producing a criterion-matched response alone. That gap stays invisible on a report until an assessment lands. Take her seriously and ask for a recent marked task rather than the grade, then look at which criterion the marks stop at. A student who says she is lost while still scoring adequately is usually right about where things are heading.

faqs.question: Can we start with online and move to home sessions later?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is a sensible order for some families. Starting online lets you judge the tutor assessment knowledge without the scheduling commitment of a home visit, and if it works you may find you never need to change. Moving to home sessions later depends on that tutor travel and their schedule for the term, so raise it early rather than assuming. Some families keep both, with one visit a week and online doubt-solving in the days before a test.

faqs.question: What should a tutor send after each session?
faqs.answer: At minimum a short note: what was covered, what the student found hard, and what to practise before the next session. For Diploma work, an annotated script or draft is more useful than a summary. This is also your main window into whether the sessions are doing anything, particularly online, so agree it in the first week rather than complaining about its absence in the second month. A tutor unwilling to send anything in writing is telling you something worth hearing.

faqs.question: Do you work with students at Lancers International School or Pathways World School?
faqs.answer: Tutors on the platform have taught students from a range of Gurugram IB campuses, and some may have worked with students at Lancers International School, Pathways World School, Scottish High International School or GD Goenka World School. That describes experience only. IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not officially affiliated with any of those schools unless specifically stated, and no tutor should ever be presented to you as school-approved or school-recommended.

faqs.question: How soon before mocks should extra sessions be booked?
faqs.answer: Earlier than feels necessary, because mock weeks are when every family in the same cohort asks at once and tutor schedules tighten. Four to six weeks ahead is comfortable for adding a session or two. Booking three days before is possible but limits the choice to whoever happens to be free. It is also worth deciding in advance whether the extra time is for content gaps or for timed practice, since those need different session shapes and sometimes different tutors.

faqs.question: What happens if progress stalls after two months?
faqs.answer: Ask a direct question first: what does the tutor think is blocking progress? A useful answer names something specific, a skill, a habit, a missing foundation from an earlier year. A vague answer is itself the finding. Beyond that, look at whether work between sessions is actually happening, since two months of good teaching with no independent practice produces exactly this pattern. If neither explains it, request a different tutor. Adding hours to a match that is not working rarely helps.
