contentBlocks.heading: What Is Checked Before a Tutor Is Put in Front of You
contentBlocks.body:
Screening covers what can actually be verified, and stops there.

Identity documents are checked. Academic qualifications are checked against the subject and level a tutor wants to teach, so someone offering Math AA HL has to show they can hold that level rather than a general mathematics background. Teaching experience is discussed in specifics: which programmes, which years, which boards or curricula before IB, and whether they have supervised internal assessment work or only classroom teaching.

A subject conversation follows. Tutors are asked how they would approach a real situation, such as a Grade 11 student whose investigation topic will not yield usable data, or a Grade 10 student who writes strong content but scores poorly against the criteria. The answers separate people who have done this from people who have read about it.

References are taken where a tutor has worked with families before. Comfort with the mode matters too, since teaching a Chemistry mechanism over a shared screen is a skill in itself and not everyone has it.

What is not claimed: that screening predicts chemistry between a particular tutor and a particular teenager. It does not. That is what the first session is for, and why an early swap is treated as normal rather than a complaint.

contentBlocks.heading: What This Platform Will Not Tell You
contentBlocks.body:
A page like this is easy to fill with promises. Here is what is deliberately absent.

No grade guarantees. Nobody who has sat with IB students for a few years will promise a 7, or a fixed jump in points, because the outcome depends on attendance, school teaching, the student's own work between sessions and how much of Grade 11 was already lost. Anyone offering a number is selling.

No tutor headcounts, no success percentages, no invented reviews. Those numbers are unverifiable and they tell you nothing useful about the one tutor who will actually sit with your child.

faqs.question: How late in the evening can a tutor come to DLF Richmond Park?
faqs.answer: Most home sessions in this part of DLF Phase 4 land between 6:00 and 8:30 pm on weekdays, and the earlier end fills first. Slots after 8:30 exist but the pool is thin, because a tutor finishing at 9:30 near Golf Course Road is looking at a long trip home afterwards. faqs.question: Is online IB tuition genuinely as good as a tutor sitting at the table?
faqs.answer: For Grade 11 and 12 it usually is, and for some things it is better. Marking a data table, annotating a proof or working through a past paper on a shared screen is cleaner than two people leaning over one printout. For a Grade 3 or Grade 6 student, the honest answer is no. Younger children need presence, and attention drifts online in a way it does not at a table. Below Grade 8 we would push you toward in person unless timing makes that impossible.

faqs.question: What do IB tutors in Gurugram usually charge, and what moves the price?
faqs.answer: Fees vary by programme, level and mode rather than by locality, so a Higher Level Diploma subject costs more per hour than PYP support, and home visits cost more than online because travel time is real time. Experience with internal assessment supervision also moves the rate. We do not publish a single figure because quoting one would be misleading. The advisor gives you the actual range for your subject, level and preferred hour before any session is arranged.

faqs.question: My son is in Grade 11 and already behind in Physics. Is it too late?
faqs.answer: It is not too late, but starting in Grade 11 is materially different from starting in Grade 12. There is still time to fix foundations, choose an investigation topic that can produce clean data, and build a paper technique across a full year. Starting midway through Grade 12, the honest work becomes triage: protect the internal assessment mark, drill the highest-yield topics, and accept that some ground will not be recovered. Both are worth doing. They are not the same job.

faqs.question: Can one tutor handle both Math AA HL and Physics HL?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking, because a single tutor across both saves a scheduling slot and the two subjects share mathematical habits. But it is not common at Higher Level. Most tutors are genuinely strong in one and adequate in the other, and adequate is not what you want in a Higher Level subject in Grade 12. If a combined match is not available at the standard you need, two specialists, one of them online, is usually the better arrangement.

faqs.question: What happens if my daughter and the tutor simply do not get along?
faqs.answer: Tell the advisor rather than the tutor, and do it in the first two or three weeks. Personality fit is the one thing screening cannot test, so a swap is treated as normal rather than as a complaint. A replacement is proposed against the same slot and level, subject to availability. The diagnostic notes from the first tutor carry over, so the new one does not restart from zero. Waiting until week ten to raise it is what actually costs you a term.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does a Diploma student near Golf Course Road usually need?
faqs.answer: Two per subject is common in the run-up to a session, but the number depends more on how much independent work the student does than on the subject itself. A student who attempts questions alone between lessons gets more out of one session than a student who only works when the tutor is present gets out of three. Many families near here run one longer weekday session and a short midweek online call for doubt-solving, which survives a busy term better.

faqs.question: Do tutors help with the internal assessment, or only exam preparation?
faqs.answer: Both, within limits. A tutor can help scope a workable investigation, question a method that will not produce analysable data, review structure against the assessment criteria and push back on a conclusion that overreaches. What a tutor must not do is write it, supply the data or draft sections. The work has to be the student's own, and schools run authenticity checks. Support that crosses that line puts the candidate at risk, so it is refused.

faqs.question: We travel often during the year. Can sessions be paused?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is better to say so at the start than to cancel repeatedly later. Some tutors will hold a slot through a two-week absence, others cannot afford to and will fill it. Online teaching is the flexible option here, since a session can continue from Delhi, Noida or from another country if the timing works. Discuss travel patterns with the advisor before matching, so you are placed with a tutor whose schedule tolerates the gaps.

contentBlocks.heading: Four Questions to Settle Before Booking an IB Tutor in DLF The Belaire, Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Most families here start the search in the wrong order. They ask who is good, then discover halfway through that the tutor teaches Standard Level well and Higher Level adequately, or that the only free hour clashes with a swimming class.

So start with four answers instead.

What exactly is the subject and level? Not "maths", but Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, or Applications and Interpretation at Standard. The two need different people. What is the next thing the school will actually mark? A criterion-assessed task in three weeks and a Diploma internal assessment draft in three months lead to completely different first sessions. Which single hour every week can this household defend against everything else? One protected hour beats three optimistic ones. And is a specialist worth taking online, given that the tutor pool inside the DLF Phase 5 radius is smaller than the pool across the city?

An advisor can work with rough answers. The point of asking them early is that they narrow the search before names appear, which is what stops a family cycling through three tutors in a term.

Everything below expands those four, in the order a parent normally needs them.
items: Subject plus level, stated precisely
The next school-marked task, with its date
One weekly hour the household can defend
Whether a specialist is worth taking online
Rough answers are fine; missing answers are not

contentBlocks.heading: How a Request From DLF The Belaire Turns Into a Confirmed Tutor
contentBlocks.body:
The sequence is short and it is worth knowing before you call, because the questions will make more sense.

An advisor takes the constraints first: grade, programme, subject, level, school and the hours available. Then the format is decided, in person or online, against what is realistically reachable in the Phase 5 area at that hour. Then tutors matching those constraints are contacted, and only the ones who confirm the exact slot are named to you. Then an introductory session runs, and only after that does anything longer get agreed.

You receive two or three names, with subject depth, levels taught and the times each can hold. Not a searchable directory, because a directory pushes the filtering work back onto a parent who has less information than the advisor does.

The introductory session is where the real assessment happens. The tutor looks at recent marked work, tests a few things that recent marks do not reveal, and writes back a short view: what is weakest, what to attack first, what will take a term rather than a fortnight. That summary belongs to you regardless of whether you continue.

One caution. A tutor who promises an outcome in that first hour has told you something useful about themselves.

contentBlocks.heading: Reading the Real Difference Between PYP, MYP and Diploma Support in Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Parents often ask for "an IB tutor" as though the three programmes were versions of one thing. They are not, and the tutor who is excellent at one can be poor at another.

Primary Years covers ages three to twelve. The work is inquiry-led, so a tutor who arrives with a folder of drill sheets undoes what the school is building. What helps is reading together, number talk, and getting a child comfortable explaining how they reached an answer rather than only producing it.

Middle Years runs ages eleven to sixteen and is where most Gurugram families first feel lost. Marks come from criteria with published descriptors, and each criterion asks for a specific behaviour. A student can answer correctly and still sit low in a band because the response never did what the descriptor described. Good MYP tutoring teaches that translation explicitly.

Diploma, ages sixteen to nineteen, is a scheduling problem wrapped around six subjects. The extended essay, theory of knowledge and the internal assessments do not queue politely. For the May 2026 and November 2026 sessions, useful support means a subject hour every week plus fixed dates for drafts, set backwards from the school's own deadlines rather than forwards from today.
items: PYP, ages 3 to 12: inquiry preserved, gaps filled quietly
MYP, ages 11 to 16: criterion descriptors drive the mark
DP, ages 16 to 19: six subjects plus EE, TOK and CAS
Draft dates set backwards from school deadlines
Support spans Grade 1 to Grade 12

contentBlocks.heading: In Person or On Screen: Picking a Format That Survives a Gurugram Term
contentBlocks.body:
The right answer changes with the child's age and the rarity of the subject, and it is worth deciding once rather than drifting.

A tutor at your dining table is the better format for younger students, for anyone who needs an adult present to stay on task, and for a parent who wants to overhear the tone of a session. The cost is fragility. Across a full term, in-person arrangements lose more hours than online ones, usually to weather, illness on either side, and evenings that run over.

On screen, the tutor can live in another city, which matters when the subject is Economics Higher Level or a language nobody nearby teaches. Screen sharing also suits mathematics: working through a solution on a tablet, with the file saved and sent afterwards, gives a student something to revise from that a whiteboard at home does not.

Many families settle on both. The taught hour happens in person on a weekend or an early evening, and a shorter midweek call handles homework doubts and quick checks on a draft.

Blunt version: choose in person for presence, online for expertise, and both when the timetable is tight.
items: In person: presence, supervision, a parent within earshot
Online: reach, reliability, saved worked solutions
Hybrid: taught hour in person, short doubt call midweek
Term-long attendance is usually higher online
Rare Higher Level subjects favour the screen

contentBlocks.heading: Maths AA or AI, and the Other Level Choices That Decide Which Tutor You Need
contentBlocks.body:
The single most consequential question in a Diploma tutoring request is not the subject. It is the level and route.

Analysis and Approaches is the algebraic, proof-facing route. Higher Level adds the deeper optional paper, and students who prepared only through routine exercises meet that paper badly. Applications and Interpretation moves the weight toward modelling, data and technology, and marks are lost in the written justification of a result rather than in the manipulation. A tutor comfortable with one route can be genuinely weak in the other, so ask directly.

Physics and Chemistry share a different pressure point. The internal assessment is one investigation, and the research design decides how much of the mark is reachable before any data is collected. Reviewing that plan early is worth more than months of content revision.

Economics and English A come down to language. Command terms are instructions, not decoration. Evaluate expects a judgement supported both ways. Examine expects the assumptions pulled apart. Students who read them as polite variations on "write about" lose marks steadily and never see why. That is the habit a tutor for these subjects should be attacking in the first month.

Math AI HL and SL: modelling, data handling, written justification
Physics and Chemistry: research design caps the investigation mark
Economics: diagram accuracy plus evaluation that goes both ways
English A: command terms read as instructions
Ask a prospective tutor which route and level they actually teach

contentBlocks.heading: Checks Run on a Tutor Before a Name Reaches You
contentBlocks.body:
Verification is bounded. Here is what it does and does not cover.

Identity is confirmed against documents. Qualifications are checked against the specific level a tutor asks to teach, so an offer to take Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level has to be backed by evidence of working at that level, not by a general degree in mathematics. Experience is discussed concretely: which programmes, how many cohorts, which curricula they taught before IB, and whether they have supervised internal assessment work or only delivered lessons.

Then a subject conversation. A tutor might be asked how they would handle a student whose Higher Level maths marks are fine on routine questions and collapse on the deeper paper, or a Middle Years student whose writing is strong but whose criterion scores are not. The response tells you whether they have met the problem before.

References are taken where earlier family work exists. Comfort with online delivery is checked separately, because explaining a titration or a proof through a shared screen is its own skill.

What verification cannot do is predict rapport. Screening filters for competence. Only the first session tests fit, which is why an early change of tutor is expected rather than resisted.

Grade and programme. Subject and level, stated exactly. The date of the next school-marked task. The one hour a week you can hold. If you also have a recently marked script, send it, because a marked script shows a tutor where the marks are leaking in a way that no description manages.

And if the student has a view about what they want fixed first, bring that too. Teenagers who chose the priority themselves argue with the plan far less in week five.

faqs.question: Should my child take Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, and can a tutor help decide?
faqs.answer: A tutor can help you think it through, but the school's advice and the child's intended university course matter more. Analysis and Approaches suits students heading toward engineering, physics, mathematics or economics degrees that expect calculus. Applications and Interpretation suits students who reason well with data and modelling but find abstract proof draining. A useful first session tests which style the student is actually stronger in, rather than which one sounds more impressive on a transcript. Decide before Grade 11 settles if you can.

faqs.question: What should I ask a prospective IB tutor on the very first call?
faqs.answer: Ask which level they teach regularly, not which they are willing to teach. Ask how many cohorts they have taken through the internal assessment for this subject. Ask what they would do in the first three sessions, and listen for whether the answer is specific. Ask how they will report back to you, and how often. Finally ask what they would need from the school. A tutor who wants the assessment calendar and a marked script is planning; one who only wants a start date is not.

faqs.question: Is it possible to move from Higher Level to Standard Level midway, and does the tutoring change?
faqs.answer: Schools do allow level changes within their own deadlines, and it is a decision to take with the school's coordinator rather than with a tutor. If it happens, the tutoring changes considerably. Content narrows, the deeper optional paper disappears in mathematics, and the work shifts toward securing full marks on what remains rather than covering more ground. It is often the right call for a student carrying three Higher Level subjects who is drowning in one of them.

faqs.question: How does IB tuition compare in price to CBSE tuition in Gurugram?
faqs.answer: It generally sits higher, because the pool of tutors who genuinely know the assessment model is smaller and Higher Level subjects need real depth. Within IB, the price moves with programme, level and format: Primary Years support costs less per hour than a Higher Level Diploma subject, and home visits carry a premium over online because travel is unpaid working time. introSummary: IB tutors in DLF The Icon Gurugram teach students from Grade 1 to Grade 12 across the Primary Years, Middle Years and Diploma programmes, at home in the surrounding Phase 5 area or online across the city. The most common misunderstanding among families here is that an IB mark measures correctness. It does not. It measures a response against a published criterion or command term, which is why a strong student can hand in accurate work and still sit in a middle band for a whole year.

contentBlocks.heading: The Assumption That Costs DLF The Icon Families a Year of IB Marks
contentBlocks.body:
A parent calls in October, usually in Grade 10 or Grade 11, and says some version of the same thing. My child knows the material. The teacher agrees the answers are right. The grade is still a 4 or a 5.

That is not a knowledge problem. It is a reading problem, and it comes from carrying an assumption over from a board system where marks track correctness fairly directly.

IB does not work that way. In the Middle Years Programme, work is judged against four criteria, each with descriptors that ask for a particular behaviour: analysis, justification, evaluation, communication of process. A factually perfect answer that never justifies anything is a factually perfect answer sitting in a low band. At Diploma, the same logic arrives as command terms. Describe and explain and evaluate are three different instructions with three different mark ceilings, and a student who reads all three as "write what you know" has capped themselves.

So the honest first job of a tutor here is often not teaching content at all. It is teaching a student to read the question as an examiner wrote it.

That takes a few weeks, not a few days, and it is the change parents notice first.
items: Correct content, middle band: the most common complaint we hear
MYP criteria reward specific behaviours, not accuracy alone
Command terms at Diploma set the mark ceiling
Technique work usually precedes content work
Noticeable shift takes weeks rather than days

contentBlocks.heading: Subject by Subject: What Tutors Near DLF The Icon Are Asked For Most
contentBlocks.body:
Economics is the request that surprises people. Families assume it is the soft option in a Higher Level block and discover that the diagrams are the easy half. The marks live in evaluation: taking a policy, arguing its effect, then arguing the limits of that effect with a real example attached. Students who write one-sided answers score consistently in the middle no matter how much theory they know.

Mathematics splits by route. Analysis and Approaches asks for algebraic control and proof, and Higher Level students meet an additional deeper paper that rewards unfamiliar problems. Applications and Interpretation asks for modelling and interpretation, where the mark often sits in the sentence explaining what the model means rather than in the calculation.

Physics and Chemistry hinge on the single investigation that forms the internal assessment. If the research design cannot produce data worth analysing, the ceiling is set before the student begins.

English A rewards close reading over summary, and the oral assessment catches students who prepared content but not delivery.

Across all of them, the same request comes up: match by level, not by subject name. A tutor strong at Standard Level is not automatically the right person for Higher Level in the same subject.
items: Economics: evaluation and counter-argument carry the marks
Math AA HL: proof plus the deeper optional paper
Math AI: modelling with the interpretation written out
Physics and Chemistry: research design decides the investigation ceiling
English A: close reading, plus preparation for the oral
Matching done at HL or SL, never by subject label alone

contentBlocks.heading: Turning a Request From DLF The Icon Into a Working Tutor Match
contentBlocks.body:
Matching starts from the diagnosis, not from a list.

An advisor asks what the last three marked pieces looked like and what the teacher's comments said, because that usually reveals whether the issue is content, technique or workload. Those need different tutors. A content gap wants a subject specialist. A technique gap wants someone who has marked against the criteria. A workload collapse wants someone organised enough to build a calendar and hold a teenager to it.

Then the practical constraints go in: grade, programme, level, the school's next deadline, the hours the family can hold, and whether the session happens at home or on a screen. Tutors who fit are approached, and only those who confirm the specific slot are named.

You get two or three options with their background and available times, then an introductory session before any longer arrangement.

After that session the tutor writes back with a plain view of what is wrong and what the first month will target. If two tutors would suit equally, the tie-breaker is usually reliability of the slot rather than the resume, because a brilliant tutor who reschedules twice a month is worth less than a solid one who never does.

Each of those calls for a different kind of tutor

Slot reliability breaks ties between similar candidates

contentBlocks.heading: Moving From MYP Year 5 to the Diploma Programme in Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
The gap between the last year of the Middle Years Programme and the first year of Diploma is the steepest step most students here meet, and it catches families who were comfortable until then.

The Middle Years Programme runs to age sixteen and grades against criteria, with a fair amount of teacher scaffolding. The Diploma Programme, from sixteen to nineteen, removes much of that scaffolding, adds Higher Level depth in three subjects, and stacks the extended essay, theory of knowledge and internal assessments across two years that also contain university applications.

Students who coped by working hard the night before stop coping in Grade 11. That is not a comment on ability. It is arithmetic: six subjects times regular deadlines does not fit into short bursts.

The useful window is the months either side of that transition. Consolidating mathematics before Higher Level begins, learning to read command terms, and building a weekly work routine cost far less effort then than repairing them in Grade 12 while the May 2026 or November 2026 session approaches.

Primary Years support, for ages three to twelve, is a different job again: reading, number sense and the confidence to explain a method out loud without a worksheet in front of them.

contentBlocks.heading: How Tutors Are Screened Before Any Family Is Introduced
contentBlocks.body:
The checks are narrow on purpose, because a broad claim about vetting is usually an empty one.

Identity documents are verified. Academic credentials are matched to the level being offered, which means a tutor asking to take Higher Level Economics has to show work at that level rather than a general background in the subject. Teaching history is discussed in specifics: which programmes, how many years, what they taught before IB, and whether they have handled internal assessment or extended essay support in a school setting.

The subject conversation is the part that filters hardest. A tutor may be asked to explain how they would raise a Middle Years student stuck in the middle band despite accurate work, or how they would help a Diploma student whose Economics essays never reach a judgement. Vague answers here end the process.

Where a tutor has taught families before, references are requested. Online teaching ability is treated as a separate competence and checked separately.

One honest caveat. None of this predicts whether a particular tutor and a particular fifteen-year-old will work well together. That is decided in the first session, which is exactly why the first session exists and why changing tutors early carries no penalty.
items: Identity and credential verification against the level offered
Teaching history discussed programme by programme
Filtering questions on criterion marking and evaluation writing
References sought where prior tutoring exists
Fit determined by the first session, not by screening

contentBlocks.heading: Choosing Between Home and Online Sessions Around DLF The Icon
contentBlocks.body:
Home tutoring gives you presence. A younger child stays on task, a parent hears how the hour is going, and the tutor sees the desk, the phone and the actual working conditions, which sometimes explains more than any diagnostic test.

Online gives you reach and consistency. The tutor can be in another city, so subject depth stops depending on geography, and a session survives rain, a late meeting or a blocked road. For mathematics and the sciences the shared screen also produces an artefact: annotated solutions the student can revisit, which a hurried notebook page rarely delivers.

The weaknesses are equally real. Online loses younger students, who need someone physically beside them. Home tutoring loses hours across a term to cancellations and to the travel margins nobody counts at the start.

Most Diploma families around here run a mixed week once they have tried both, with the taught hour in person and a shorter screen call for doubts, draft checks and a run through past paper questions attempted alone.

If the choice has to be made in one line: teach younger children in the room, and choose Diploma tutors on subject strength regardless of where they sit.
items: In person: attention, supervision, visible working conditions
Online: subject reach, fewer lost sessions, saved annotated work
Weak point of online: students below roughly Grade 8
Weak point of home visits: hours lost across a full term
Mixed week common for Grade 11 and Grade 12

No predicted outcome. Nobody will tell you the child will reach a 6 or gain three points, since results depend on classroom teaching, attendance, independent work and how late the help began. Anyone attaching a number to it is guessing in a confident voice.

faqs.question: Why did my child's MYP grade stay low when the answers were correct?
faqs.answer: Because the criteria reward particular behaviours rather than correctness alone. A response can be accurate and still miss the analysis, justification or evaluation the descriptor asks for, and it lands in a middle band as a result. Students who move up are usually the ones who learn to read the criterion before writing, then check their draft against each strand. This is teachable, it takes a few weeks of deliberate practice, and it is often where a tutor adds the most value early on.

faqs.question: Is Economics an easy Higher Level subject to take?
faqs.answer: It is often chosen on that assumption and it disappoints people. Diagrams and definitions are manageable, and they are not where the marks separate students. Higher bands need evaluation: a judgement, supported, with the limits of that judgement acknowledged and a concrete example behind it. Students who write everything they know about a policy score middling answers reliably. The internal assessment adds its own demand, since commentaries have to connect real news articles to theory within a tight word limit.

faqs.question: Do we need a separate tutor for theory of knowledge?
faqs.answer: Usually not a weekly one. Theory of knowledge is taught in school and the assessment is an essay on a prescribed title plus an exhibition, so most students need targeted help at two or three points rather than continuous teaching. A few sessions on framing a knowledge question, structuring an argument and using examples properly tend to be enough. If a student is genuinely lost with the subject as a whole, a short block of sessions early in Grade 12 works better than spreading it thin.

faqs.question: My child moves from MYP Year 5 into the Diploma next year. What should we do now?
faqs.answer: Use the months before Grade 11 rather than waiting for a problem. Consolidate mathematics to the level the chosen route expects, since gaps there widen quickly at Higher Level. Practise reading command terms and writing to them. Build a weekly routine, because six subjects with rolling deadlines break students who work in bursts. If the subject choices are not final, a diagnostic session can indicate where the student is genuinely stronger, which is more useful than choosing by reputation.

faqs.question: Can a CBSE or A-Level tutor teach IB subjects effectively?
faqs.answer: Subject knowledge transfers. Assessment knowledge often does not, and that is where IB marks are decided. A tutor unfamiliar with criterion descriptors, command terms or internal assessment requirements can teach content well and still leave a student scoring the same as before. Ask directly how many IB cohorts they have taught and whether they have supervised internal assessment work. Some tutors from other systems have made the shift properly, but it should be evidenced rather than assumed.

faqs.question: How do predicted grades work, and can tutoring influence them?
faqs.answer: Predicted grades are issued by the school, based on the teachers' judgement of a student's likely performance, and they matter for university applications. Nobody outside the school sets them and no tutor should suggest they can. What tutoring can do is improve the evidence teachers are looking at: mock results, internal assessment quality and classwork. That is an indirect route and it needs time, which is why families aiming at strong predicted grades usually start in Grade 11 rather than after they arrive.

faqs.question: We are near DLF Phase 5. Are weekday evening in-person slots realistic?
faqs.answer: For mathematics, the sciences, Economics and English, generally yes, because tutors already work along this stretch of Golf Course Road. Between roughly 6:00 and 8:00 pm is the busiest band, so flexibility on the exact start time helps. For rarer subjects or second languages, in-person weekday slots are genuinely scarce and waiting for one can cost a term. Online is the practical answer in those cases. Everything depends on tutor schedules and is confirmed when the request is made.

faqs.question: What if there is no visible progress after a month?
faqs.answer: Raise it with the advisor and ask for the tutor's own account of what has and has not shifted. Sometimes the plan is right and the marked assessment simply has not happened yet. Sometimes the diagnosis was wrong, and what looked like a content gap is a workload or motivation problem needing a different approach. Sometimes the tutor is not the right fit. All three are common, all three are fixable, and none of them improve by waiting another two months.

faqs.question: Can the same tutor teach two children at different levels?
faqs.answer: It works when the levels are close, for instance two Middle Years students in adjacent years, and it saves scheduling effort. It works poorly when one child is in Grade 8 and the other is sitting a Higher Level Diploma subject, since those need different expertise and different session lengths. Shared sessions between siblings are rarely a good idea beyond the primary years, because the pace ends up wrong for at least one of them. Discuss the specific ages with the advisor.

mainEntity.name: Why did my child's MYP grade stay low when the answers were correct?

acceptedAnswer.text: Because the criteria reward particular behaviours rather than correctness alone. A response can be accurate and still miss the analysis, justification or evaluation the descriptor asks for, and it lands in a middle band as a result. Students who move up are usually the ones who learn to read the criterion before writing, then check their draft against each strand. This is teachable, it takes a few weeks of deliberate practice, and it is often where a tutor adds the most value early on.

mainEntity.name: Is Economics an easy Higher Level subject to take?

acceptedAnswer.text: It is often chosen on that assumption and it disappoints people. Diagrams and definitions are manageable, and they are not where the marks separate students. Higher bands need evaluation: a judgement, supported, with the limits of that judgement acknowledged and a concrete example behind it. Students who write everything they know about a policy score middling answers reliably. The internal assessment adds its own demand, since commentaries have to connect real news articles to theory within a tight word limit.

mainEntity.name: Do we need a separate tutor for theory of knowledge?

acceptedAnswer.text: Usually not a weekly one. Theory of knowledge is taught in school and the assessment is an essay on a prescribed title plus an exhibition, so most students need targeted help at two or three points rather than continuous teaching. A few sessions on framing a knowledge question, structuring an argument and using examples properly tend to be enough. If a student is genuinely lost with the subject as a whole, a short block of sessions early in Grade 12 works better than spreading it thin.

mainEntity.name: My child moves from MYP Year 5 into the Diploma next year. What should we do now?

acceptedAnswer.text: Use the months before Grade 11 rather than waiting for a problem. Consolidate mathematics to the level the chosen route expects, since gaps there widen quickly at Higher Level. Practise reading command terms and writing to them. Build a weekly routine, because six subjects with rolling deadlines break students who work in bursts. If the subject choices are not final, a diagnostic session can indicate where the student is genuinely stronger, which is more useful than choosing by reputation.

mainEntity.name: Can a CBSE or A-Level tutor teach IB subjects effectively?

acceptedAnswer.text: Subject knowledge transfers. Assessment knowledge often does not, and that is where IB marks are decided. A tutor unfamiliar with criterion descriptors, command terms or internal assessment requirements can teach content well and still leave a student scoring the same as before. Ask directly how many IB cohorts they have taught and whether they have supervised internal assessment work. Some tutors from other systems have made the shift properly, but it should be evidenced rather than assumed.

mainEntity.name: How do predicted grades work, and can tutoring influence them?

acceptedAnswer.text: Predicted grades are issued by the school, based on the teachers' judgement of a student's likely performance, and they matter for university applications. Nobody outside the school sets them and no tutor should suggest they can. What tutoring can do is improve the evidence teachers are looking at: mock results, internal assessment quality and classwork. That is an indirect route and it needs time, which is why families aiming at strong predicted grades usually start in Grade 11 rather than after they arrive.

mainEntity.name: We are near DLF Phase 5. Are weekday evening in-person slots realistic?

acceptedAnswer.text: For mathematics, the sciences, Economics and English, generally yes, because tutors already work along this stretch of Golf Course Road. Between roughly 6:00 and 8:00 pm is the busiest band, so flexibility on the exact start time helps. For rarer subjects or second languages, in-person weekday slots are genuinely scarce and waiting for one can cost a term. Online is the practical answer in those cases. Everything depends on tutor schedules and is confirmed when the request is made.

mainEntity.name: What if there is no visible progress after a month?

acceptedAnswer.text: Raise it with the advisor and ask for the tutor's own account of what has and has not shifted. Sometimes the plan is right and the marked assessment simply has not happened yet. Sometimes the diagnosis was wrong, and what looked like a content gap is a workload or motivation problem needing a different approach. Sometimes the tutor is not the right fit. All three are common, all three are fixable, and none of them improve by waiting another two months.

mainEntity.name: Can the same tutor teach two children at different levels?

acceptedAnswer.text: It works when the levels are close, for instance two Middle Years students in adjacent years, and it saves scheduling effort. It works poorly when one child is in Grade 8 and the other is sitting a Higher Level Diploma subject, since those need different expertise and different session lengths. Shared sessions between siblings are rarely a good idea beyond the primary years, because the pace ends up wrong for at least one of them. Discuss the specific ages with the advisor.

finalCta: Describe what the last marked assignments looked like and what the teacher wrote, then give the grade, subject, level and the hours you can hold weekly. An advisor will confirm what is available near DLF The Icon, share the fee range, and set up a diagnostic session before anything longer is agreed.

contentBlocks.heading: The Distance Between a Predicted Grade and a May Result at DLF The Pinnacle
contentBlocks.body:
A predicted grade is a school's professional judgement, submitted to universities long before any paper is opened. The final grade is what an examiner in another country awards after reading a script. Between those two moments sits most of an academic year, and that stretch is the only part a tutor can genuinely affect.

Families looking for IB tutors in DLF The Pinnacle Gurugram normally arrive holding one of those numbers and worrying about the other. The gap is commonly a point, sometimes two. It is rarely a question of ability. It is usually a small set of repeatable errors: an internal assessment that was submitted before the criteria were read properly, a Paper 2 answer that describes when the command term said evaluate, working shown in a way that forfeits method marks.

So the useful first conversation is not about tutors at all. It is about evidence. Bring the last marked script, the school report with the predicted grades on it, and the IA feedback sheet if one exists.

From there the plan becomes narrow and checkable. One subject at a time, one habit at a time, with the school's own deadline calendar setting the order of work rather than a generic syllabus schedule.

contentBlocks.heading: At Home in DLF The Pinnacle or Online: What Actually Works on a Gurugram Weeknight
contentBlocks.body:
Home sessions have a real advantage that is easy to underrate. The tutor sees the desk, the textbook pile, the phone lying face up, and the calculator the student has not learned to drive. Diagnosis improves when you can look at the workspace.

The cost is travel. A tutor coming from Sushant Lok or Sector 57 on a weekday evening is exposed to Golf Course Road at its worst, and a 6.30 pm slot has a habit of becoming 6.50. That matters less for a ninety-minute Chemistry session than for a forty-five minute doubt-clearing slot, where a fifth of the session can disappear before anyone sits down.

Online suits three situations here. Late slots after 8.30 pm, when a student returns from a match or a rehearsal. Rare combinations, where the right specialist may not live within a sensible drive of DLF Phase 5. And revision fortnights before the May session, when short, frequent contact beats long weekly blocks.

Many households run both. Weekend sessions at home for the subject that needs the most supervision, midweek online for everything else. Whether a particular tutor can offer either mode near DLF The Pinnacle depends on their schedule and can be reviewed before you commit.

Evening traffic on Golf Course Road erodes short slots more than long ones

contentBlocks.heading: The IB Subjects That Move a Prediction Most for Students Near DLF The Pinnacle
contentBlocks.body:
Physics and Chemistry at Higher Level generate the steadiest demand from this part of DLF Phase 5, and for a specific reason. Both courses accelerate sharply in the second term of DP1, and a student who is coping in October can be visibly behind by February without anything dramatic having happened.

In Physics HL the loss is often mathematical rather than conceptual. Students understand the idea and then mishandle the algebra under time pressure, or quote an answer without a unit. In Chemistry HL the internal assessment is the usual pressure point, because it is marked on the quality of the investigation and the treatment of uncertainty, not on whether the numbers came out neatly.

Mathematics splits the enquiries. Math AA HL is proof-heavy and punishing in Paper 3; Math AI HL rewards modelling and statistics, and students who chose it expecting relief are often caught out by the data work.

Economics and English A come up regularly too. Economics marks leak in the evaluation paragraphs, where students restate rather than judge. English A pressure tends to concentrate around the individual oral. Rarer subjects such as Psychology or a language ab initio are usually easier to match online than within a short drive.

contentBlocks.heading: PYP, MYP and DP: When Grades Start Being Recorded and Predicted
contentBlocks.body:
The three IB programmes hold very different expectations, and the word grade means something different in each.

The Primary Years Programme, roughly ages three to twelve, is organised around units of inquiry and closes with the exhibition in the final year. Nothing here is being predicted to anybody. Tutoring that helps at this stage builds reading stamina, number sense and the willingness to say an idea out loud. Converting it into worksheet drilling works against the programme.

The Middle Years Programme covers ages eleven to sixteen and is assessed against criteria A to D, each scored one to eight, with descriptors rather than percentages. Students moving in from a board school find this genuinely disorienting: careful, thorough work can still score modestly because the criterion asked for something the student never addressed. MYP 5 also carries the personal project.

The Diploma Programme is where predictions arrive and start mattering. Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus an extended essay of about four thousand words, theory of knowledge, and CAS. The EE and TOK combination contributes up to three points on the matrix out of a total of forty-five. Examinations run in the May and November sessions, and the internal deadlines that feed them sit much earlier.

MYP: criteria A to D scored one to eight, plus the personal project in MYP 5

contentBlocks.heading: How a Shortlist Gets Built for a Household in Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Matching starts with a call, and the call is mostly questions. Which programme year. Which subjects and at what level. What the last two reports said. Whether the problem is one subject or a scheduling collapse across five.

Then the constraints get written down honestly. A DP2 student with school until 3.15 pm, sport twice a week and an IA due in three weeks has perhaps four usable evening hours. Planning six is how families end up cancelling by the fourth week and concluding tutoring does not work.

Only after that does IB Gram look at people. Tutors are filtered on the exact level first, because Math AA HL and Math AI SL are different jobs. Then on assessment experience: has this person actually supervised an Economics IA through to submission, or only taught the content. Then on the practical fit, which means travel time to DLF Phase 5, the slot the family can hold, and language of instruction if that matters.

You are given a small shortlist rather than a directory, with the reasoning attached. A short introductory session can usually be arranged so the student meets the tutor before any longer commitment, subject to tutor availability.

Assessment experience checked separately from teaching experience
Realistic weekly hours agreed before the schedule is drawn
Travel time to DLF Phase 5 treated as a hard constraint, not a preference
Short introductory session where the tutor's schedule allows it

contentBlocks.heading: What Four Weeks Should Visibly Change, and What It Will Not
contentBlocks.body:
Set a checkpoint at the end of the first month, and be concrete about what you are looking for.

Reasonable to expect by then: the student can explain what a command term is asking before answering it. Past-paper attempts are being written under timing rather than open-book. The IA has a defined research question and a data plan instead of a vague topic. Homework arguments at home have reduced in frequency, because somebody outside the family now owns the schedule.

Not reasonable to expect by then: a two-point jump in a Higher Level subject. Predicted grades move when a body of evidence moves, and schools update them on their own cycle, usually after an internal examination series. A tutor cannot shortcut that, and any tutor who promises a specific final grade is telling you something they cannot know.

An honest warning about starting late. A student beginning in February of DP2 with three weak Higher Level subjects will have to choose. Spreading four hours a week across all three usually produces small movement everywhere and a decisive change nowhere. Picking the two subjects that matter for the university offer is uncomfortable, and it is generally the better call.

contentBlocks.heading: What Gets Checked Before a Tutor Reaches Your Gate in Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Screening happens before a name is put in front of a family, and it is deliberately unglamorous.

Identity is confirmed against government photo identification. Qualifications are verified against the actual certificate rather than a claim on a profile. IB teaching or tutoring experience is checked at the level being claimed, because a tutor who has taught Standard Level for years may never have taken a student through Higher Level Paper 3.

Assessment familiarity is treated as a separate question. The screening asks how the person would structure a Physics IA from a weak research question, or what they would tell a student whose Economics evaluation reads as description. Answers to that kind of question separate genuine IB experience from general subject knowledge quickly.

For home sessions the practical checks matter too: verifiable contact details, a stated service radius that honestly includes DLF Phase 5, and willingness to be registered at the society gate as a recurring visitor.

What screening cannot do is guarantee chemistry between a particular tutor and a particular fifteen-year-old. If the fit is wrong, say so early, and a different profile can be reviewed rather than persisting out of politeness.
items: Government photo ID confirmed before any introduction
Certificates seen, not just claimed on a profile
Experience verified at the specific level, HL and SL treated separately
Scenario questions on IA supervision and command-term coaching
Service radius and gate registration confirmed for home visits

Start with a short conversation rather than a booking. An advisor asks for the programme year, the subjects and their levels, the current predicted grades, and the deadlines the school has already set. Fifteen minutes is usually enough to tell whether the problem is one subject or the whole week.

You are then sent a small shortlist with reasons attached, not a list of everybody available. Each profile states the level experience, the assessment work the tutor has actually supervised, and whether home sessions in DLF Phase 5 are realistic given their existing schedule.

One ninety-minute sitting with a past paper and the last IA draft tells an experienced tutor more than a month of general revision, and it gives you something concrete to judge before extending the commitment. faqs.question: Are there IB tutors who can travel to DLF The Pinnacle for home sessions?
faqs.answer: Home tutoring around DLF The Pinnacle can often be arranged, though it depends entirely on which tutor suits the subject and level and what their existing schedule looks like. Tutors travelling from DLF Phase 1, DLF Phase 4 or Sushant Lok generally accept slots here more readily than those based towards Sohna Road or Sector 65. Availability for a specific evening slot can be reviewed once the subjects and preferred timings are known. faqs.question: What determines how much an IB tutor costs in Gurugram?
faqs.answer: Four things move the fee. Level comes first, because Higher Level work and Paper 3 preparation demand a narrower kind of experience than Standard Level teaching. Subject scarcity comes second: Math AA HL, Physics HL and less common options cost more than widely taught subjects. Session length and frequency matter, and so does mode, since home visits carry travel time the tutor cannot use. Rates are quoted before anything is confirmed, and you should never be settling a fee after a tutor has already reached your door.

faqs.question: My son is predicted a 4 in Physics HL. Is a 6 realistic by the May session?
faqs.answer: It depends almost entirely on when you start and what the 4 is made of. If the marks are being lost to algebraic slips, missing units and unfinished Paper 2 questions, that is mechanical and responds well to disciplined timed practice. If the underlying concepts in fields and quantum are genuinely absent, the work is longer. No honest tutor will promise you a grade. What can be promised is a diagnostic on the last marked script and a candid statement of what the remaining months can and cannot cover.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Chemistry internal assessment without it becoming academic misconduct?
faqs.answer: Yes, within clear limits. A tutor can teach how a research question is narrowed, how variables are controlled, how uncertainty is propagated and what the assessment criteria actually reward. They can read a draft and point out where the evaluation is thin. What they must not do is write text, supply data, or produce the analysis for the student. Your school will have its own authenticity declaration, and any tutor working on an IA should be operating well inside it. Ask directly at the first session where they draw the line.

faqs.question: We live near Sector 43 but the school run goes towards Sohna Road. Does that complicate matching?
faqs.answer: It affects timing more than it affects choice. A long school commute means the student reaches home later, so early evening slots become unreliable and the weekend carries more of the load. Tutors are matched against the hours you can genuinely hold rather than the hours that look tidy on paper. In practice families in this situation often keep one longer weekend session at home in DLF Phase 5 and move midweek doubt-clearing online, which removes travel from both sides of the arrangement.

faqs.question: What happens if the first tutor turns out to be the wrong fit?
faqs.answer: Say so early rather than waiting for a term to end. Fit problems usually show inside three sessions and they are rarely about competence: pace, tone and the student's willingness to admit confusion all matter. Raise it with your advisor, describe what specifically is not working, and a different profile can be reviewed against the same requirement. Changing once is normal. Changing repeatedly usually points at something other than the tutor, such as the schedule being unrealistic or the wrong subject having been prioritised.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring genuinely as good as sitting in the same room for HL Mathematics?
faqs.answer: For Higher Level Mathematics it is often better, provided the setup is right. Written work needs to be visible, so a tablet with a stylus or a document camera pointed at the page is close to essential; audio alone does not work for a proof. Once that exists, screen-shared past papers and a shared whiteboard let the tutor watch the working develop in real time. What online loses is the incidental supervision of a home session, which matters more for younger MYP students than for DP candidates.

faqs.question: Should a DP1 student start now, or wait until DP2 begins?
faqs.answer: Starting in DP1 is usually cheaper in total hours and calmer for everyone. The second term of DP1 is when most subjects accelerate, and it is also when the internal assessment cycle begins in several courses. A student who fixes command-term habits and IA structure that year enters DP2 needing revision rather than repair. Waiting is defensible if DP1 grades are steady and the family wants to see the first internal examination series before committing. Waiting until February of DP2 forces hard choices between subjects.

mainEntity.name: Is online tutoring genuinely as good as sitting in the same room for HL Mathematics?

acceptedAnswer.text: For Higher Level Mathematics it is often better, provided the setup is right. Written work needs to be visible, so a tablet with a stylus or a document camera pointed at the page is close to essential; audio alone does not work for a proof. Once that exists, screen-shared past papers and a shared whiteboard let the tutor watch the working develop in real time. What online loses is the incidental supervision of a home session, which matters more for younger MYP students than for DP candidates.

mainEntity.name: Should a DP1 student start now, or wait until DP2 begins?

acceptedAnswer.text: Starting in DP1 is usually cheaper in total hours and calmer for everyone. The second term of DP1 is when most subjects accelerate, and it is also when the internal assessment cycle begins in several courses. A student who fixes command-term habits and IA structure that year enters DP2 needing revision rather than repair. Waiting is defensible if DP1 grades are steady and the family wants to see the first internal examination series before committing. Waiting until February of DP2 forces hard choices between subjects.

contentBlocks.heading: Comparing Two IB Tutors Properly: The Questions Families at DLF Trinity Towers Skip
contentBlocks.body:
Two profiles land in your inbox. Both say ten years of IB experience. Both quote similar fees. Both sound confident on the phone. Almost every parent then decides on tone of voice, and about a third of those decisions get reversed within six weeks.

There are four questions that actually discriminate between candidates, and none of them is about years.

First: which level, precisely. A tutor with a decade of Standard Level Mathematics behind them may never have prepared a candidate for Math AA HL Paper 3. Ask for the level and the paper, not the subject.

Second: what have they supervised, as opposed to taught. Reading a syllabus is not the same as steering an internal assessment from a vague research question to a submitted report.

Third: what do they do when a student is silent. Some tutors fill the silence and leave with the session feeling productive and nothing transferred. Ask how they check that understanding has moved.

Fourth: can they hold the slot. A brilliant tutor who cancels twice a month is worse than a competent one who never does.

Families searching for IB tutors in DLF Trinity Towers Gurugram get more from those four answers than from any amount of profile prose.
items: Level and paper named exactly, not the subject in general
Internal assessments supervised to submission, with the subject stated
How the tutor tests that understanding has actually shifted
Cancellation and rescheduling history over a full term
Willingness to be judged on written work rather than session feel

contentBlocks.heading: How IB Gram Narrows a Gurugram Shortlist Down to Two or Three Names
contentBlocks.body:
Matching runs as a sequence of filters, each one applied before the next, so that the final comparison is between candidates who are already equivalent on the things that are not negotiable.

Step one is the level filter. Programme year, subject, and level. Math AI SL and Math AA HL do not share a shortlist.

Step two is the assessment filter. If the family's pressure point is an IA draft due in three weeks, tutors without documented IA supervision in that subject come out of the pool, however strong their teaching record.

Step three is the schedule filter, and it is the one families resist. You state the hours you can genuinely hold, allowing for school timings, sport and travel. Anything that requires a household to reorganise itself permanently tends to collapse by the fifth week.

Step four is geography. For an address in DLF Phase 5 that means a tutor whose stated service radius honestly covers Golf Course Road, not one who will attempt it twice and then ask to move online.

What reaches you is two or three profiles with the reasoning written out. A short introductory session can usually be arranged before any longer arrangement, depending on the tutor's schedule.

contentBlocks.heading: Math AA, Math AI and the Rest of the Subject Board in Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Mathematics dominates enquiries from this stretch of DLF Phase 5, and the two routes reward completely different tutors.

Analysis and Approaches is the algebraic road. Higher Level candidates face three papers, with Paper 3 running as a long, structured investigation that asks students to extend an idea rather than repeat a method. Proof by induction, complex numbers and calculus depth sit here. A tutor who is comfortable in AA SL can be visibly out of their depth in AA Paper 3, and it shows within two sessions.

Applications and Interpretation goes the other way. Modelling, statistics, hypothesis testing, and a heavy reliance on the graphic display calculator. Students who chose AI to avoid proof frequently discover that the statistical inference is where their marks go. Both routes carry the mathematical exploration, an internally assessed piece of around twenty pages that is marked on personal engagement and mathematical communication as much as on difficulty.

Beyond Maths, Physics and Chemistry at Higher Level are the usual requests, then Economics and English A. For scarcer choices such as Business Management or Global Politics, the pool near Golf Course Road is thin and online matching is usually the sensible route.

Math AI HL: modelling, statistical inference, calculator fluency
The mathematical exploration, marked on engagement and communication
Physics HL and Chemistry HL as the next tier of demand
Economics and English A for essay-technique work
Scarce subjects matched online rather than by postcode

contentBlocks.heading: Primary Years to Diploma: What Each Stage Asks of a Tutor
contentBlocks.body:
The comparison between two tutors changes shape depending on which programme your child is in, because the job itself is different.

For a Primary Years Programme child, the right tutor is a patient generalist. Learning runs through units of inquiry and ends with the exhibition in the final year. What you want is someone who can build reading stamina and number confidence without turning the week into worksheets. Subject expertise counts for less than temperament at this stage.

For a Middle Years Programme student, the tutor needs to read criteria. Assessment sits against criteria A to D, each on a one to eight scale, with published descriptors. A student can produce careful work and still score in the middle because the criterion asked for analysis and received description. MYP 5 adds the personal project, which is largely a project management problem wearing academic clothes.

For a Diploma candidate, the tutor is a specialist and nothing less. Six subjects, three at Higher Level, an extended essay of roughly four thousand words, theory of knowledge with its exhibition and prescribed title essay, and CAS alongside. EE and TOK together offer up to three points on the matrix, from a maximum of forty-five, with examinations in the May and November sessions.
items: PYP: temperament over specialism, inquiry units and the exhibition
MYP: criteria A to D on a one to eight scale, plus the MYP 5 personal project
DP: subject specialism, three Higher Levels, EE, TOK and CAS
Core points: up to three from the EE and TOK matrix out of forty-five
May and November sessions, with internal deadlines well ahead of them

The Rapid Metro runs the length of that corridor, which changes who will accept a slot: tutors who do not drive can reach this address without turning an hour of teaching into three hours of their evening.

contentBlocks.heading: Home, Online or Both for Households at DLF Trinity Towers
contentBlocks.body:
When you compare two tutors, mode is not a detail to settle afterwards. It changes which of them is actually better for your child.

A home session buys supervision. For a Middle Years student who drifts the moment nobody is in the room, that supervision is most of the value, and a tutor who is merely good but physically present will outperform an excellent one on a screen.

An online session buys specialism and punctuality. A Diploma candidate working on a Math AA HL exploration needs someone fluent in exactly that, and the person who fits may live nowhere near Golf Course Road. Online also removes the traffic risk on the tutor's side, which is why late evening slots after 8.30 pm are far easier to hold online than in person.

The requirement for online Mathematics or Physics is a writing surface the tutor can see. A tablet with a stylus, or a phone on a stand angled at the page, does the job. Voice alone does not, and any tutor who says otherwise has not taught a proof remotely.

Hybrid weeks are the common compromise near DLF Trinity Towers: one supervised session at home, the rest online, adjusted at revision time.

contentBlocks.heading: The Checks Sitting Behind a Tutor Profile in Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
A profile is only worth comparing if the claims on it have been tested. Screening covers four things, and it is done before a name is sent to a family.

Identity is confirmed against government photo identification, with contact details that resolve to a real person. Academic qualifications are checked against certificates rather than accepted from a form. Teaching history is verified at the level claimed, which is where a good number of applications stop, because Higher Level experience is asserted far more often than it exists.

The fourth check is practical and harder to fake. Applicants are asked how they would handle specific situations: an exploration with no personal engagement in it, a student whose Paper 2 answers describe when the command term said discuss, a Chemistry IA with data that did not behave. Vague answers here are informative.

For home visits, the stated service radius is confirmed and has to include DLF Phase 5 honestly, not aspirationally.

None of this guarantees rapport. Screening can establish competence and reliability. It cannot predict whether a particular teenager will talk to a particular adult, which is why the first three sessions matter and why raising a mismatch early is sensible rather than rude.
items: Government photo identification and verifiable contact details
Certificates inspected, claims not taken at face value
Level-specific teaching history checked separately from total years
Scenario questions on explorations, command terms and awkward IA data
Honest service radius covering DLF Phase 5 for home sessions

contentBlocks.heading: Judging Value After the First Month, Not the First Session
contentBlocks.body:
The first session almost always feels good. The tutor is attentive, the student is on best behaviour, and nothing has been tested yet. Judge at week four instead.

By then you should be able to see specific things in the student's own work. Solutions with the working laid out in a way that would earn method marks. Past-paper attempts done under timing rather than with the textbook open. An exploration or IA with a defined question and a plan for the data, not a topic and good intentions. Fewer arguments at home about when work will start, because somebody else now owns the schedule.

What you should not expect at week four is a changed predicted grade. Schools revise predictions on their own assessment cycle, typically after an internal examination series, and no tutor can move that timetable or promise where it lands. Any specific score promised to you is a claim nobody is in a position to make.

One genuine limitation. Tutoring cannot repair a subject choice that was wrong from the start. A student who took Math AA HL for university admissions reasons and struggles with algebraic fluency may be better served by a level change than by four hours a week, and a sensible tutor will say so early.

Timed past-paper attempts replacing open-book practice
Exploration or IA with a fixed question and a data plan
Predicted grades move on the school's cycle, never on request
A wrong level is a level problem, not a tutoring problem

contentBlocks.body:
Begin by sending three pieces of information: the programme year, every subject with its level, and the nearest deadline. That is enough for an advisor to tell whether you need a specialist for one subject or a schedule for all six.

You then receive a small set of profiles, each with the level experience, the assessment work actually supervised, and a plain statement of whether home sessions at your address in DLF Phase 5 are realistic given that tutor's existing week. Where schedules allow, a short introductory session can be arranged so the student meets the person before anything longer is agreed.

Fees are quoted at that stage, by level, mode and session length, so the comparison is between complete propositions rather than half of one.

One more thing worth agreeing at the start: how you will both know it is working. Settle on the evidence in advance. Timed past papers marked against the real scheme. A redrafted exploration. A topic the student could now teach back to you. Vague reassurance at week four helps nobody, and it is much harder to argue with a marked script.

If you want a single practical suggestion: give both shortlisted tutors the same marked script and the same twenty minutes. The difference in what they notice will tell you more than any interview. Availability remains subject to tutor schedules.

faqs.question: Two tutors both claim ten years of IB experience. How do I tell them apart?
faqs.answer: Ask each for the levels and papers they have prepared candidates for, by name. Then ask how many internal assessments they have supervised to submission in that subject, and what the weakest one looked like at draft stage. Finally ask what they would do in the first session with your child's last marked script. Specific, unhesitating answers indicate genuine work at that level. Long generalities about passion and methodology usually indicate teaching experience at a different level than the one you need.

faqs.question: What should I ask a Math AA HL tutor during the introductory session?
faqs.answer: Ask how they would approach a Paper 3 investigation, since that paper rewards extending an unfamiliar idea rather than reproducing a method. Ask what they look for in the mathematical exploration, and whether they can name the criteria it is marked against. Ask how they build algebraic fluency in a student who understands concepts but loses marks in manipulation. Answers that stay concrete, referring to actual questions and student errors, are worth more than any description of teaching philosophy.

faqs.question: Do fees change between a Standard Level and a Higher Level subject?
faqs.answer: Usually yes. Higher Level work requires a narrower pool of tutors, particularly in Mathematics and the sciences where Paper 3 preparation and extended internal assessment supervision are involved, and scarcity is reflected in the rate. Session length, frequency and mode also matter, since a home visit in DLF Phase 5 costs the tutor travel time that an online slot does not. All of it is quoted before you confirm anything, and nothing should be agreed after a session has already been taught.

faqs.question: Can we use one tutor for Mathematics and a different one for Physics?
faqs.answer: That is common and often better than looking for someone who claims both at Higher Level. Genuine depth in Math AA HL and in Physics HL rarely sits in the same person, and a tutor stretched across both tends to be strong in one and adequate in the other. The practical cost is coordination: two schedules, two sets of feedback, more calendar management for you. Where the week is already tight, families sometimes keep one subject at home and run the second online to reduce the scheduling load.

faqs.question: Our flat is on the Sector 54 side of DLF Phase 5. Which areas do tutors travel from?
faqs.answer: Realistically from DLF Phase 1, DLF Phase 4, Sushant Lok, Sector 53 and the nearer parts of Golf Course Road, where the run is short and reasonably predictable. Tutors based around Sohna Road, Sector 65 or Nirvana Country can reach DLF Trinity Towers but generally prefer earlier slots, and a late weekday start from that direction is an unreliable arrangement. Where geography does not work but the tutor is the right match on level and assessment experience, online sessions solve it cleanly.

faqs.question: How many hours a week does a DP2 student taking Math AI HL usually need?
faqs.answer: Two sessions a week is the common pattern once the exploration is submitted, often ninety minutes each, with one weighted towards content and one towards timed past papers. Before submission the balance shifts, and a stretch of shorter, more frequent contact around the draft deadline works better than a single long block. What matters more than the number is consistency across the term. Four hours in one week and none the next produces less than two steady hours every week.

faqs.question: What if the school moves an internal assessment deadline midway through?
faqs.answer: Schools do this, and a tutoring plan should be able to absorb it. Tell your advisor and the tutor as soon as the new date is announced, because the order of work changes rather than the total quantity. Typically the exploration or investigation moves to the front of the queue for two or three weeks and content teaching pauses, then resumes once the draft is submitted. Rescheduling a session or converting a home slot to online at short notice is usually possible, depending on the tutor's other commitments.

faqs.question: Is the introductory session charged?
faqs.answer: It depends on the tutor and the format agreed. Some offer a short unpaid conversation intended for the student and tutor to meet and for the family to ask questions. A full diagnostic session, where the tutor works through a marked script and produces a written assessment of what is going wrong, is normally chargeable because it is real work. Whichever applies is stated before it happens, and you should decline any arrangement where the cost of the first session is left unclear.

introSummary: Families looking for IB tutors in DLF Wellington Estate Gurugram usually start in October or February, and the month matters more than they expect. An August start buys habit repair and extended essay planning. A February start in DP2 buys triage and exam technique, and very little else.
