faqs.question: How many sessions before we can tell whether this is working?
faqs.answer: Four is a fair review point, and the thing to examine is process rather than marks. By then a student should be attempting questions in a different order, showing working the tutor has insisted on, or planning an extended response before starting to write it. Marks tend to move later, after the next round of school assessments. If nothing about how the student works has shifted by session four, raise it. A tutor who cannot describe what has improved is not really diagnosing.

faqs.question: Our daughter is in Math AI SL and the school has suggested moving to Analysis and Approaches. Should we?
faqs.answer: It depends on where the mathematics is going after school rather than on which course looks easier. Analysis and Approaches suits students heading towards engineering, physics or mathematics-heavy economics, and some universities specify it outright. Applications and Interpretation suits students who will use statistics and modelling rather than proof. Switching upward mid-course is demanding, because AA assumes algebraic fluency that AI never drills. Speak to the school first, then arrange a diagnostic session before committing, since the right answer is genuinely individual.

faqs.question: The internal assessment deadline is three weeks away and the draft is a mess. What now?
faqs.answer: Triage, with a realistic ceiling. In three weeks a tutor can help the student read the criteria properly, identify which sections are actually losing marks, and restructure the argument so the evidence already gathered does more work. What cannot happen is a fresh investigation or a rewrite by somebody else, since that crosses academic honesty rules and schools do check. Expect improvement rather than transformation. Opening the IA conversation two months out produces a far better result than opening it three weeks out.

faqs.question: What internet and desk setup does an online session actually need?
faqs.answer: Less than people assume, though the basics matter. A connection stable enough to survive an hour, a laptop or tablet with a working camera placed so the tutor can see the page being written on, and a desk in a room with a door that closes. A phone propped against a book fails for mathematics and the sciences, because the tutor needs to watch working develop line by line. Headphones help in a busy flat. Most homes in these sectors already have everything needed.

faqs.question: Our child needs help across six subjects, not one. Is that even possible?
faqs.answer: Possible, though rarely with one person teaching all six. What usually works better is a specialist for the one or two subjects that are genuinely weak, combined with a planning session covering the whole timetable: deadlines mapped out, revision blocked, and the internal assessments sequenced so they do not all land in the same fortnight. Diploma students seldom fail on content across six subjects simultaneously. They fail on scheduling, and scheduling is a much cheaper problem to solve.

contentBlocks.heading: IB Tutors in Mayfield Garden, Gurugram: What the School Run Actually Looks Like
contentBlocks.body:
Four international schools pull children out of Mayfield Garden every morning, and they do not share a calendar. Lancers International School sits on the Golf Course Road side. Scottish High International School is out in Sector 57. Pathways World School and GD Goenka World School draw from the Sohna Road direction. Internal assessment deadlines, mock windows and school reporting cycles are set by the school, not by the neighbourhood, so two children living in the same tower can be under completely different pressure in the same fortnight. A tutor who is genuinely useful here has to work around the school's calendar rather than a generic tuition timetable.

So the first question is rarely which subject. It is which school, which programme year, and what the next three deadlines are. IB Gram takes those details first, then looks at who is free during the hours a Mayfield Garden household can actually protect. Some of those slots exist locally. Some only exist online. contentBlocks.heading: Subject Requests That Send Mayfield Garden Families Looking for a Tutor
contentBlocks.body:
Math AA HL is the single most common request from this pocket of Gurugram, and it is also where a mismatch shows up fastest. A tutor comfortable with Class 12 board calculus is not automatically comfortable with proof-style questions, the calculator paper, or the exploration a DP student has to produce independently. Math AI HL needs a different person again: more statistics, more modelling, more interpretation of context that arrives wrapped in a real-world scenario.

Physics and Chemistry requests tend to arrive in two waves. The first is conceptual, usually in MYP or DP Year 1, where the student can follow the lesson but cannot start a question on their own. The second is procedural and lands closer to the exam: data booklet fluency, significant figures, and reading what the command term is actually asking for.

Economics sits apart from both. Most students who lose marks in it are not weak on content. They are writing paragraphs that never connect a diagram to an evaluation, and the repair is editorial more than conceptual.

English A is usually requested late, after a first individual oral or a written task comes back lower than expected. Work there resembles close reading practice rather than grammar drilling, and it takes several weeks to show up in a grade. An IB science tutor in Mayfield Garden and an English A tutor are rarely the same person.
items: Math AA HL: proofs, paper 2 calculator work, the exploration
Math AI HL: statistics, modelling, context-heavy questions
Physics and Chemistry: concept gaps early, technique gaps late
Economics: diagram-to-evaluation links, not content recall
English A: close reading, oral commentary, written task structure

contentBlocks.heading: How a Shortlist Is Built for a Mayfield Garden Address
contentBlocks.body:
A shortlist for a Mayfield Garden address is built in five steps, and none of them begin with browsing profiles.

One. The intake call records the school, the programme year, the exact subject and level, and the assessment that is closest. HL Chemistry with an IA due in five weeks is a different brief from HL Chemistry in September.

Two. The subject requirement is separated from the scheduling requirement. Families often discover at this point that their real constraint is a 45-minute window on Tuesdays, not the subject at all.

Three. Tutors are filtered on IB experience at that level, then on availability during the hours you named, then on travel feasibility from wherever they are based.

Four. Two or three names go out with what each has actually taught, described in their own words rather than reduced to a rating. If only one tutor fits, you are told that.

Five. The first session runs as a diagnostic. The tutor works through recent school work and a few past-paper questions to find where marks are being dropped, then writes a short plan.

Availability moves week to week, so a name that fits in March may not fit in July. Nothing here should be read as a promise that a particular tutor is free. What can be promised is a quick answer when the match is not there.
items: School, year, subject, level and nearest deadline recorded first
Scheduling constraint separated from subject constraint
Teaching history shared in the tutor's own words
Diagnostic first session, not a sales session
A direct no when nothing suitable is free

contentBlocks.heading: PYP, MYP and DP Needs Across Mayfield Garden, Malibu Towne and Suncity
contentBlocks.body:
Support across Grade 1 to Grade 12 does not mean the same thing at every stage, and parents in this pocket ask for very different things depending on where their child sits.

In the Primary Years Programme, roughly ages three to twelve, the useful work is reading fluency, number sense, and helping a child explain their thinking out loud. Turning a unit of inquiry into a worksheet routine defeats the point and tends to reappear later as a student who cannot begin an open question.

The Middle Years Programme, ages eleven to sixteen, is where most of the frustration lives. A child understands the science and still lands in the middle band, because the assessment is criterion-related and the response never addresses the criterion the way the rubric asks. Work here often starts with reading the task sheet properly before writing anything.

The Diploma Programme, ages sixteen to nineteen, brings the deadlines that dominate a household: internal assessments across six subjects, the extended essay, TOK, and mock papers. Students who begin support in DP Year 1 have room to plan. Students who begin in January of DP Year 2 are triaging, and it is fairer to say so at the start than after two months.

May 2026 and November 2026 sessions both matter around here, since schools in this belt do not all sit the same one.
items: PYP: inquiry, reading fluency, explaining reasoning aloud
MYP: criterion language and task-sheet comprehension
DP: six IAs, extended essay, TOK, mock cycles
Grade 1 to Grade 12 covered, with different aims per stage
May 2026 and November 2026 both in play locally

contentBlocks.heading: What Is Checked Before a Tutor Is Recommended Anywhere in Gurugram

IB Gram is an independent service with no formal standing with the IB, Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel. Any workshop history or examining experience a tutor mentions belongs to them personally and is reported as they describe it.

Feedback after the first few sessions is taken seriously. Where the fit is wrong, a change is arranged rather than argued about.

contentBlocks.heading: Home, Online or Both for IB Tuition in Mayfield Garden, Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Home tutoring works in Mayfield Garden when three things line up: the tutor is based nearby, the slot avoids the worst of the Sohna Road evening, and the subject is common enough for a local match to exist. Maths and the sciences usually clear that bar. Availability still depends on tutor schedules and can be reviewed before you plan a term around it.

Online is not the fallback it is often assumed to be. For DP Year 2 revision, for a rarer subject combination, or for a 9pm slot after a late activity, it is frequently the better option, because you are choosing from tutors across Gurugram instead of tutors within a few kilometres. Screen-shared past papers annotate more cleanly than a shared notebook on a dining table.

The honest trade-off is attention. A twelve-year-old who drifts within ten minutes of a video call will do better in the room with someone. Younger PYP and early MYP students generally learn more face to face, whatever the convenience argument says.

Hybrid is where most DP families in this pocket land: one weekend session at home for the longer piece of work, one weekday session online for doubt-solving and quick corrections. It keeps travel cost down without giving up the in-person time that makes harder conversations easier.

Home availability subject to tutor schedules

contentBlocks.heading: Fees, Tutor Changes and the Real Limits of IB Tutoring in Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Fees are not published as one number, and any page quoting a single figure is guessing. Rates move with subject, level and format. HL Physics costs more per hour than MYP Maths because fewer people teach it well. Online usually sits below home tutoring, since the tutor is not absorbing travel time. You are given a range for your specific request before anything is booked, and the shortlist itself carries no charge.

Changing a tutor is a normal request, not a complaint. If the first match is wrong, say so after two or three sessions instead of waiting out a term. Fit is hard to predict from a profile, which is exactly why the opening session is diagnostic.

Now the limitation, stated once and clearly. Tutoring cannot recover a term of missed school work in four weeks. It cannot write an internal assessment. It cannot guarantee any grade, and nobody honest will offer you one.

What it can do is make the next fortnight's work land properly. A reasonable checkpoint is four to six weeks: better structure in written answers, fewer blank starts on past-paper questions, homework going in on time. If none of that has moved, the plan needs changing, and that conversation should come from the tutor before you have to raise it.

Online typically lighter than home tutoring on fees
Tutor changes handled after two or three sessions if needed
No grade guarantees, ever
Four to six week checkpoint on structure and consistency

faqs.question: Can a tutor actually reach Mayfield Garden on a weekday evening?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it depends heavily on where the tutor starts from. Someone based around Sector 45 to 47, Malibu Towne or Suncity can usually manage a 6pm or 7pm slot. Someone coming from the DLF phases or Sector 57 is fighting Sohna Road at exactly the wrong hour, and those requests are often declined rather than accepted and then cancelled later. Weekend mornings and afternoon slots after school are far easier to fill. All home visits remain subject to tutor availability at the time you ask.

faqs.question: My child studies at Scottish High in Sector 57. Does the tutor need to know that school?
faqs.answer: Knowing the school helps more than most parents expect. It tells the tutor which term the assessment weeks fall in, how the school sequences a subject across DP Year 1 and Year 2, and roughly how much homework already exists on a Tuesday night. It does not mean the tutor has any connection to the school. IB Gram is an independent platform with no affiliation to Scottish High International School or any other school named on this page. faqs.question: What does IB tuition near Mayfield Garden usually cost?
faqs.answer: There is no single rate, and a page that publishes one is inventing it. Fees vary by subject, by level, and by whether the tutor travels. HL sciences and HL Maths sit at the higher end because the pool of people who can teach them properly is small. MYP and PYP support sits lower. Online is generally cheaper than a home visit, since nobody is paying for an hour lost on Sohna Road. You get a range for your exact request before booking, and the shortlist costs nothing.

faqs.question: Is an online tutor genuinely workable for Math AA HL?
faqs.answer: For DP students, usually yes, and often better. Past papers and mark schemes can be shared on screen and annotated live, worked solutions stay legible, and the recording of a tricky proof can be revisited before a mock. The bigger gain is choice: you are selecting from IB Maths specialists across Gurugram rather than the handful who can drive to Mayfield Garden by seven. Where online struggles is with younger students who lose focus quickly. For a sixteen-year-old working towards an exam session, that is rarely the issue.

faqs.question: We are starting in January of DP Year 2. Is that too late to help?
faqs.answer: It is late, but not pointless. What changes is the goal. You are no longer building understanding from the ground up. You are protecting the internal assessment that still has marks available, drilling the paper structure, and picking the topics where the return per hour is highest. A tutor should tell you in the first session which parts are realistically recoverable before the May session and which are not. If someone promises a full turnaround in eight weeks, treat that as a warning sign rather than reassurance.

faqs.question: How is an IB tutor different from a regular CBSE tutor?
faqs.answer: The content overlaps far more than the assessment does. A CBSE tutor may know the physics perfectly and still cost a student marks, because IB questions are graded against command terms and criteria that reward a specific kind of response. Explain, evaluate, justify and describe all mean different things and earn different marks. Add internal assessments, the extended essay and TOK, none of which exist in the same form on a board syllabus, and the gap becomes practical rather than theoretical. Matching is done on IB experience at the level required.

faqs.question: What happens if we see no progress after a month?
faqs.answer: Raise it, and expect the tutor to raise it first. The first session should have produced a written note with a target, so there is something concrete to compare against rather than a general feeling. Sometimes the fix is a change of approach, more past-paper work and less teaching from the front. Sometimes the fit is simply wrong and a different tutor is arranged. Occasionally the honest answer is that the number of sessions is too low for the amount of ground being covered, and that needs saying too.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover the extended essay and TOK alongside a subject?
faqs.answer: It depends on the essay's subject. An extended essay in Economics is best supervised by someone who teaches Economics, since the research question has to be answerable within that subject's methods. TOK is different again and often suits a tutor with a humanities or philosophy background. Some tutors handle both comfortably. Many do not, and will say so. Where one person cannot cover everything, the sensible arrangement is a subject tutor for the weekly work and separate, shorter sessions for the extended essay milestones.

faqs.question: Do you support MYP students around Mayfield Garden, or only the Diploma Programme?
faqs.answer: Both, across Grade 1 to Grade 12. MYP requests from this area are steady and usually sound the same: the child understands the topic but the criterion-based marks stay stuck in the middle band. That work is about reading the task sheet, planning against each criterion, and writing a response the rubric can actually reward. PYP support is available too, though it looks nothing like tuition at the older end. It is reading, number confidence and getting a child comfortable explaining how they reached an answer.

contentBlocks.heading: Exam-Season Rescue or a Plan: IB Tutors in Nirvana Country, Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Most families around Nirvana Country get in touch in one of two states. The first is February or April, three weeks out from a mock or an internal assessment deadline, and the message begins with the word urgent. The second is July, when the year has only just started and nothing has gone wrong yet.

The July call produces better outcomes. It is not close.

Exam-season work is triage. There is time to repair technique, not understanding. A tutor can show a DP student how to read command terms, how to structure a Paper 2 response, and which topics still hold recoverable marks. They cannot rebuild two years of Chemistry in five weeks, and anyone who suggests otherwise is selling rather than teaching.

Year-long support looks different from the inside. Weekly sessions track what the school is covering that fortnight, catch a misunderstanding in September instead of March, and leave enough room for the extended essay to be planned rather than rescued. The weekly hours are usually lower. Across a full year the total spend is often lower too, because nobody is buying fifteen emergency sessions inside a single month.

Both are arranged for families here. What follows describes what each one actually involves.
items: July start: lower weekly hours, more room to plan
April start: technique and mark recovery, not new understanding
Emergency blocks cost more per week than steady support
Extended essay planned early rather than salvaged late

contentBlocks.heading: Home Visits and Online Sessions Around Nirvana Country and South City 2
contentBlocks.body:
Nirvana Country, Unitech Fresco and Unitech The Close sit close enough together that a tutor already booked in one can often add a second slot nearby the same evening. That density is why home tutoring here is more feasible than in the outer sectors, at least for the common subjects and at least outside the worst of the Sohna Road rush.

Online earns its place for different reasons. A student revising for a November session needs frequent short contacts more than long weekly ones, and a 30-minute doubt-solving call on a Thursday night is only practical when nobody is driving. Past papers annotate well on a shared screen. So does an IA draft, which is difficult to review properly while sitting side by side with one laptop.

The drawback is real and worth naming. Online suits students who can hold attention for an hour without a person in the room. Many can. Some cannot, and for those students a home session is simply the better spend, whatever the timetable says.

A common pattern from this pocket: one longer home session at the weekend for the heavy work, then two short online check-ins during the week when deadlines cluster. Home availability depends on tutor schedules and can be reviewed before you commit to a term.

Short midweek online calls for doubt-solving

Weekend home session plus midweek online check-ins

contentBlocks.body:
Economics generates a surprising share of requests from this side of Sohna Road, and the diagnosis is nearly always the same. The student knows the definitions. Their paragraphs describe a diagram and then stop, without the evaluation the mark scheme is waiting for. Fixing that is about writing discipline, and it moves faster than most parents expect.

Chemistry is slower. Losses usually trace back to one unresolved idea from an earlier topic, and until that is found, extra past papers just repeat the same error more efficiently. A good first session hunts for that root cause instead of covering new ground.

Math AI HL trips students who chose it expecting an easier route than AA. The statistics and modelling content is genuinely demanding, and the written interpretation carries marks that pure calculation does not. AA HL requests centre on proofs and on the exploration.

English A shows up in the second half of DP Year 1, usually after an oral or a written assignment lands below expectation. Progress there is measured in weeks, not sessions.

Physics sits between the two extremes: conceptual early, then a technique problem about uncertainties, graph work and command terms. An IB maths tutor in Nirvana Country and a Physics specialist are rarely interchangeable, even though families often assume they are.

Chemistry: one buried misconception behind repeated errors
Math AI HL: statistics and written interpretation

Physics: uncertainties, graph work, command term precision

contentBlocks.heading: The IB Year Month by Month for Gurugram Families
contentBlocks.body:
Grade 1 to Grade 12 is a wide span, so it helps to look at the calendar rather than the age band.

A Primary Years Programme child has no external deadlines at all. Support at that stage is about reading stamina, number confidence and the habit of explaining an answer out loud. It should feel like conversation, not like a tuition class, and it works best in short sittings spread across the week.

Middle Years Programme students hit their first real crunch in the second and third terms, when criterion-marked assignments stack up. The recurring problem is a strong answer written against the wrong criterion. Fixing that is a reading exercise before it is a subject one.

Diploma Programme students live by a fixed sequence. DP Year 1 runs from settling into six subjects through to the first serious internal assessment work and an extended essay research question by the year's end. DP Year 2 opens with IA drafts, moves into mocks in the new year, then final papers. May 2026 and November 2026 sessions divide students in this belt, and a November candidate is roughly six months behind a May one on that same track.

Starting late is allowed. It just narrows what a tutor can sensibly promise to attempt.
items: PYP: short, frequent sittings, no external deadlines
MYP: criterion misreading peaks in terms two and three
DP Year 1: subject grounding, IA groundwork, EE question
DP Year 2: drafts, mocks, then final papers
November candidates run about six months off the May track

contentBlocks.heading: From First Call to First Session for a Nirvana Country Family
contentBlocks.body:
The first conversation is short and mostly about facts. Which school, which programme year, which subject and level, what the last piece of feedback said, and which two or three hours in the week are genuinely free. That last answer shapes the shortlist more than anything else.

Within a day or two, two or three tutor profiles come back. Each carries what that person has actually taught at that level and where, written the way they described it. There are no star ratings, because a rating averaged across unrelated students tells you nothing about your child's HL Economics paper.

You choose. Then the first session runs as a diagnostic: recent school work reviewed, a few past-paper questions attempted under something close to real conditions, and a written note at the end covering what is solid, what is not, and what the next four sessions will target.

After three or four weeks there is a checkpoint conversation. Either the note's targets are moving or the plan changes.

One caveat. Tutor availability shifts constantly, particularly in the weeks around mocks, so a shortlist reflects that week rather than a standing roster. If nothing suitable is free for your slot, you are told directly instead of being offered a poor fit.

Shortlists reflect that week's availability only

contentBlocks.heading: Fees, Cancellations and What Cannot Be Promised in Nirvana Country, Gurugram

HL sciences and HL Maths carry the highest rates because very few people teach them to a standard that helps at that level. MYP support costs less. Online costs less than a home visit for the same tutor, since travel time is not being paid for.

You receive a range for your exact request before anything is confirmed. Preparing the shortlist itself is free.

Cancellations need a rule agreed in advance rather than negotiated in the moment. Reasonable notice on either side, a session rescheduled rather than lost where possible, and an honest conversation if a tutor is cancelling often. Repeated last-minute changes are grounds to switch, and switching is treated as routine.

And the limits. No grade is guaranteed here, by anyone, for any subject. No tutor writes an internal assessment or an extended essay. Nothing on this page reports success rates or student outcomes, because those numbers cannot be substantiated. What a family should expect to see in four to six weeks is more structured written work, fewer questions abandoned unattempted, and deadlines being met without a scramble.

faqs.question: Should we begin tutoring in July or wait until closer to the mocks?
faqs.answer: July, if the choice is genuinely open. Starting with the school year means a tutor can follow what is being taught, catch a misunderstanding while the class is still on that topic, and build towards internal assessment deadlines instead of chasing them. Waiting until January restricts the work to exam technique and topic triage, which helps but helps less. There is also a scheduling argument. Good tutors fill their evening slots early in the year, and the choice available in July is wider than the choice available in February.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week make sense for a DP student?
faqs.answer: For steady year-long support, one session per subject per week is usually enough, with occasional short calls when a deadline lands. Two subjects at that rate is manageable alongside school. Three starts eating the evenings a student needs for their own revision, and that is counterproductive. During the four to six weeks before mocks, the pattern flips: shorter, more frequent sessions built around past papers work better than long ones. A tutor who recommends more hours without a reason tied to specific marks is worth questioning.

faqs.question: Can sessions pause during school holidays or family travel?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is better to plan the pause than to cancel week by week. Tell the tutor the dates at the start of the month so the plan is built around them rather than disrupted by them. Long breaks in DP Year 2 are worth thinking about carefully, since a three-week gap in January sits right where mock preparation should be. Some families keep one short online session running through travel purely to maintain rhythm. Others stop entirely and accept a slower restart.

faqs.question: Is home tutoring realistic here, or is this an online-only area?
faqs.answer: Home tutoring is realistic for the common subjects, helped by how tightly Nirvana Country, Unitech Fresco and Unitech The Close sit together. A tutor can often serve two households in one trip, which makes the travel worthwhile. It gets harder for HL sciences and rarer subject combinations, where the pool of qualified people is small and may not include anyone living nearby. For those, online usually gives a better teacher. Every home booking depends on tutor schedules at the time you enquire.

faqs.question: What is realistic to attempt for a November 2026 session?
faqs.answer: A November candidate has roughly six extra months compared with the May track, and that time is genuinely useful if it is used from the start rather than from September. The sensible plan front-loads internal assessment work into the earlier months, then keeps the final stretch clear for past papers and paper technique. For a retake, the honest first step is a diagnostic on the previous paper: which components lost marks, and whether those marks were lost on understanding or on execution. The answer changes the plan completely.

faqs.question: What happens if a tutor keeps cancelling at short notice?
faqs.answer: Raise it after the second time rather than the fifth. A one-off change is normal, particularly around school examination duty. A pattern is not, and it costs a student more than the missed hour, since the rhythm of weekly work is what makes tutoring effective. A replacement can be arranged, and doing so is treated as an ordinary request rather than a dispute. Agreeing notice periods and reschedule rules at the very first session prevents most of these conversations from becoming awkward later.

faqs.question: My child is in MYP and the grades will not move. What would actually change?
faqs.answer: Usually the writing, not the studying. MYP marks are awarded against specific criteria, and a well-informed answer that never addresses the criterion the task names will sit in the middle band no matter how much revision goes in. The first thing a tutor should do is read the last two graded tasks alongside the rubric and show the student the gap. From there, the work is planning a response against each strand before writing. Results tend to appear over a term rather than in a fortnight.

faqs.question: Will a tutor help choose the extended essay research question?
faqs.answer: They can advise on whether a question is answerable, appropriately narrow and supported by sources the student can actually reach. That is legitimate guidance and it saves months of wasted effort. What a tutor must not do is choose the question outright, supply the argument, or draft sections of the essay. The supervisor at school owns the formal process, and any tutoring should sit alongside it rather than compete with it. Honest support here mostly looks like hard questions about scope and evidence.

faqs.answer: No. IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not officially affiliated with any of the schools named unless specifically stated. Nor is it connected to the International Baccalaureate Organization. Schools are referenced because knowing where a student studies helps a tutor plan around real assessment weeks and homework loads. contentBlocks.heading: How the Shortlist Is Actually Built for an Orchid Island Address
contentBlocks.body:
Short answer: an advisory call, then two or three named profiles with reasons, usually inside a working day or two.

The longer version runs to four steps and skips none of them.

One, we take specifics. Subject, level, year group, school, and the most recent piece of marked work. Vague briefs breed vague matches, so the more precisely you can say what is failing, the better the shortlist reads.

Two, we sort on assessment experience. For a Diploma request that means asking whether a tutor has supported internal assessments in that subject and understands moderation, not simply whether they have covered the content.

Three, we test timing against reality. A tutor who agrees to seven o'clock on a Wednesday but lives out past Sector 57 will be crossing the Sohna Road junctions at precisely the wrong hour. Far better to establish that now than in week three.

Four, the shortlist arrives with written reasoning and you choose from it.

If the first choice does not work, the list is rebuilt without argument and without charge. Changing early costs far less than persisting with a poor fit, and an advisor who resists that request is protecting the wrong interest.

contentBlocks.heading: Command Terms, Not Chapters: Subject Help Near Orchid Island, Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Short answer: Math AA HL, Math AI HL, Physics, Chemistry, Economics and English A are the subjects requested most from this belt.

The more useful answer concerns where marks are lost, and it is usually the command term rather than the chapter.

In Chemistry, a student who calculates confidently still drops marks because a question said deduce and the answer merely stated. In Economics, evaluate is not a synonym for explain, and a response that describes two policies without weighing them caps itself well below full marks however neat the diagrams are. Physics questions asking a student to justify want the reasoning written down, not implied by a correct final figure.

English A behaves the same way. Analyse asks how a text produces its effect. A great many students answer what the text says, which is comprehension, and it scores accordingly.

Mathematics is the partial exception. There the loss is normally method marks left unwritten, particularly in Analysis and Approaches at higher level, where the working carries much of the available credit.

An IB science tutor near Orchid Island worth booking will mark one of your child's answers against the command term in front of you and show exactly where it stopped scoring.
items: Chemistry: deduce against state, and the marks it costs
Economics: evaluate needs weighing, not two descriptions
Physics: justify wants the reasoning written out
English A: analyse how, rather than report what
Mathematics: unwritten method marks, especially in AA HL

contentBlocks.heading: Which IB Programme Your Child Is In Changes the Answer Completely
contentBlocks.body:
Short answer: PYP, MYP and DP need three different kinds of tutor, and hiring the wrong kind quietly wastes a term.

A Primary Years Programme parent is usually worried about reading fluency or confidence with number. What helps is short, frequent, playful work with somebody who will not convert a Grade 3 child into a worksheet machine. What does not help is a Diploma specialist filling an hour because that was the slot going spare.

Middle Years Programme students need a tutor who can read a criterion descriptor and translate it into something actionable. Criterion levels run on an eight-point scale, and the recurring pattern is solid knowledge sitting beside weak communication or thin inquiry. That is a coaching problem about structure and planning, and it moves fast once somebody names it out loud.

Diploma students need subject depth and calendar management in roughly equal measure. Higher level content, internal assessments, the extended essay and theory of knowledge all compete for the same evenings, with the May 2026 or November 2026 session waiting at the end.

Grade 1 to Grade 12 can all be supported. The error is assuming one tutor profile stretches across that range.
items: PYP: short, frequent sessions that protect curiosity
MYP: criterion descriptors translated into actions
DP: subject depth alongside calendar management
May 2026 and November 2026 as the fixed horizon
A different tutor profile at each stage

contentBlocks.heading: Three Ways to Run the Week From an Orchid Island Flat
contentBlocks.body:
Short answer: home, online, or one of each per week. All three are workable from this address.

Home tuition is the usual request and, unusually for Gurugram, a realistic one here. IB home tuition in Orchid Island, Gurugram is easier to arrange than in the outer sectors because the tutor catchment sits so close. Younger students and anyone who needs an adult in the room benefit most from it.

Online changes what is available rather than what is convenient. contentBlocks.heading: Straight Answers About Fees, Guarantees and Changing Tutors

Short answers here, because these are the questions parents hesitate to ask on a call.

Fees are not published as a single rate, because there is not one. They move with level, with how rare the subject is, and with mode. No grade is guaranteed. Not a 7, not a band, not a percentage improvement. Anybody promising one is describing an outcome they do not control, since final results depend on moderation and on a student working alone in an examination hall for three hours.

Changing tutors is ordinary. Ask, and the shortlist is rebuilt. Two sessions is enough to know when a fit is wrong, and saying so is not rude.

Progress in month one shows up in method before it shows up in marks: cleaner working, planning before writing, fewer questions left blank. If a tutor cannot point at something concrete after four sessions, treat that as a signal.

And no amount of tutoring replaces the work a student does between sessions.

faqs.question: We searched for an IB tuition centre near Orchid Island. Is a centre better than a private tutor?
faqs.answer: It depends on the subject and the student. A centre suits students who need routine and who work better alongside others, and it is usually cheaper per hour. A private tutor suits anyone with a specific gap, an internal assessment to repair, or a subject combination a batch cannot address. For higher level Diploma subjects the individual route generally wins, because the problems are particular to that student's script. For general MYP support either can work. What we arrange is individual matching rather than batch classes.

faqs.question: How is IB tutoring different from the CBSE tuition our neighbours use?
faqs.answer: The content overlaps more than the assessment does. A CBSE tutor is often excellent at solving problems quickly and covering a syllabus thoroughly, which is what board examinations reward. Diploma papers reward something else: reasoning made visible, command terms answered precisely, and an internal assessment built against published criteria. A student coached purely for speed can lose marks by skipping working an IB examiner needs to see. That is why matching is done on IB experience rather than on general subject strength alone.

faqs.question: My daughter's theory of knowledge essay is due and her school supervisor is hard to reach. Can a tutor help?
faqs.answer: A tutor can help with structure, with the quality of the knowledge questions, and with checking that the essay engages with the prescribed title instead of describing examples. What a tutor must not do is supply the argument or redraft paragraphs, because theory of knowledge essays are checked and the consequences fall on the student. Keep chasing the school supervisor as well. The formal guidance is theirs to give, and there are limits on how many drafts they are permitted to comment on.

faqs.question: Is IB Gram linked to Orchid Island or its residents welfare association?
faqs.answer: No connection at all. IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform with no arrangement involving Orchid Island, its management or any residents welfare association. The society name is used because families search that way, and because location genuinely affects which tutors can reach you on a weekday evening. If entry requires a gate pass or prior registration, the tutor will follow whatever your society asks. None of the schools named on this page is affiliated with the platform either.

faqs.question: Our son takes Chemistry HL and keeps saying the tests are unfair. What is usually behind that?
faqs.answer: Normally it means the questions are not the ones he practised. Chemistry HL papers apply familiar ideas to unfamiliar contexts, so a student who revises by redoing worked examples finds the paper alien even though every topic has been covered. The remedy is past papers under time, marked against the mark scheme rather than against the textbook, so he can see which command terms he is answering wrongly. It feels unfair right up to the point where the pattern becomes visible, which usually takes a few weeks.

faqs.question: Can sessions be paused during school examination weeks?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is often sensible. Plenty of families reduce or pause through school examination weeks, then resume with a heavier schedule afterwards. Give reasonable notice so the slot is not simply lost, because a good tutor's Tuesday evening will be taken by another family within a fortnight. Some students do better keeping one short session running through the period, particularly in a subject where the tutor acts as a check on revision quality rather than teaching anything new.

faqs.question: Should sessions be sixty minutes or ninety?
faqs.answer: Sixty suits younger students and most MYP work, because attention fades and two shorter sessions a week beat one long one. Ninety makes sense for Diploma students working through past papers, where a full Paper 2 question plus a proper review does not compress into an hour. For internal assessment work, ninety is usually right. The real constraint is the evening itself: a ninety-minute session starting at seven finishes late for a student who left home at seven that morning.

faqs.question: Our child is in MYP Year 5 and starts the Diploma next year. Is there anything worth doing now?
faqs.answer: Quite a lot, and it is the cheapest tutoring anybody buys. The gap between MYP5 and DP1 is where most students lose ground, especially in mathematics, where the algebraic fluency assumed at higher level does not always survive the summer break. A few holiday sessions on algebra, on structured writing, and on how to read a mark scheme will save a term of catching up later. Subject choice conversations belong here too, before the option form goes back to school.

faqs.question: Is sharing a tutor with another child from a neighbouring flat an option?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, though it needs care. Two students from the Sector 48 to Sector 50 belt taking the same subject at the same level can share a tutor productively, and the fee is normally split between the families. The arrangement breaks down when the two are at different levels, or when one is building an internal assessment while the other revises for a class test. Ask for it at the enquiry stage so the tutor can plan for two, and expect the match to take longer to find.

contentBlocks.heading: What a week of IB study actually looks like in Orchid Petals
contentBlocks.body:
Most families searching for IB tutors in Orchid Petals Gurugram are not short of hours. They are short of shape. A Grade 9 student here often leaves before eight, gets back past four, and then chooses between a Physics worksheet, a Language and Literature reading, and football. The choice tends to go badly on the days with two activities.

So the first thing worth examining is the study habit, not the tutor. Watch what the student does in the twenty minutes after the laptop opens. If those minutes go to re-reading notes and highlighting, extra tuition will not move much. If they go to attempting one past question and marking it honestly against the criteria, a tutor becomes a multiplier instead of a crutch.

Once the habit is visible, tutor selection gets simpler. A student who cannot start work alone needs someone who builds structure and checks in mid-week. A student who works steadily but stalls on extended Paper 2 responses needs a subject specialist, possibly online, possibly for six weeks and no longer. Those are two different people with two different fee patterns.

Parents in the Sector 48 to Sector 50 pocket frequently ask for both at once. Sequencing them usually works better, and costs less.

Habit gap and subject gap need different tutors
Activity-heavy weekdays need lighter session plans

contentBlocks.heading: Maths and sciences: the subject calls that go wrong near Sector 48-50
contentBlocks.body:
The single most common mismatch we see from this pocket is the maths one. A parent asks for an IB maths tutor Orchid Petals and does not know whether the child is in Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, or at HL or SL. The two courses share a name and very little else. Math AA HL leans on proof, calculus and algebraic fluency. Math AI HL leans on modelling, statistics and interpretation of real data, and its exploration looks nothing like an AA exploration. A tutor strong in one can be mediocre in the other.

Physics and Chemistry throw up a different problem. Students often understand the content and still lose marks because they answer a "suggest" question as though it said "state". Command-term drilling is dull work, and it is where a lot of quiet marks live.

Economics needs someone who can push a student past textbook definitions into diagram accuracy and evaluation paragraphs that actually weigh two sides. English A needs a reader, not a summariser: unseen commentary work rewards close attention to a small passage.

Before asking about fees, send the exact subject line from the school report. It saves a wasted trial session.

Physics and Chemistry: command terms lose more marks than content
Economics: diagram accuracy plus real evaluation, not definitions
English A: close reading of unseen passages
Share the subject line from the school report before the first call

contentBlocks.heading: PYP, MYP and DP habits inside Orchid Petals, Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Families here span the full range, Grade 1 to Grade 12, and the useful support looks nothing alike at either end.

For Primary Years Programme children, the work is mostly reading stamina, number sense and curiosity that survives contact with a worksheet. A tutor who converts inquiry units into drill sheets is doing damage that shows up four years later. Short sessions, twice a week, are usually enough at this stage.

Middle Years Programme students hit a specific wall: they know the content and cannot present it in criterion language. A strong answer in MYP Sciences reads differently from a strong answer in MYP Individuals and Societies, and students rarely get told how. This is the stage where a tutor who has actually marked against the criteria descriptors earns their fee.

Diploma Programme students need something narrower and harder. Internal assessment direction early, before the topic is chosen badly. Extended Essay supervision that keeps the research question small enough to answer. Theory of Knowledge help that turns vague opinion into a claim with a counterclaim. And past-paper work timed properly, because DP papers punish slow starters.

Planning for the May 2026 and November 2026 sessions works best when it begins a full term earlier than feels necessary.
items: PYP: reading stamina and number sense, not worksheet volume
MYP: translating known content into criterion language
DP: IA topic choice, EE scope control, TOK claim and counterclaim
May 2026 and November 2026 planning starts a term early
Grade 1 to Grade 12 supported, with different session lengths

contentBlocks.heading: Home, online or split: what works on the Sohna Road side of Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
IB home tuition Orchid Petals Gurugram is practical when the tutor already lives or teaches on this side of the city. A tutor coming from Sector 49, Sector 50 or the South City 2 side can hold a 6:30 pm slot reliably. One travelling from the Golf Course Extension side during evening traffic cannot, and the honest outcome is a session that starts late, runs short, and quietly gets cancelled twice a month.

Online changes the arithmetic. The pool stops being "tutors who can reach Sohna Road" and becomes "tutors who know this syllabus". For Math AI HL, for a rarely chosen Group 6 subject, or for four weeks of intense DP revision before mocks, that difference matters more than the comfort of someone at the dining table.

Where online is genuinely worse: a Grade 4 child who needs a person physically pointing at the page, and a Grade 11 student who has already learned to nod at a screen while doing nothing. Both need presence.

Many families here settle on a split. One home session on a weekend morning for the harder subject, one online midweek for revision. It is not elegant, but it survives the school calendar.

contentBlocks.heading: How a shortlist for an Orchid Petals family gets built
contentBlocks.body:
The process is deliberately unglamorous. It runs in five steps.

One: an advisor takes the details that actually constrain the match. Programme, subject and level, school, current grade or predicted grade, and the three or four time windows that are genuinely free. Not aspirational windows. Real ones.

Two: the request is filtered against tutors who have taught that exact level, with IB assessment experience noted separately from general subject teaching experience. A brilliant university physicist who has never seen an internal assessment rubric is not a match for a DP Physics IA.

Three: travel feasibility is checked against Orchid Petals and the surrounding Sector 48-50 addresses if home tutoring is requested. If nobody suitable can realistically reach the flat at the time you need, we say so rather than sending someone who will drop out.

Four: a short list goes to you with subject depth, mode and fee band. Two or three names, not a directory.

Five: an introductory session. The tutor should come out of it able to name what is actually weak, in one sentence, without hedging.

All of it depends on tutor availability at the time you ask, and availability for niche HL subjects moves week to week.

contentBlocks.heading: What gets checked before a tutor is sent to a Gurugram home
contentBlocks.body:
Screening is a checklist, not a promise. Here is what it covers.

Identity and background details are collected and confirmed before any home visit is arranged. Teaching history is checked against the programme claimed, so an application saying "IB experience" is pushed to specify which programme, which subjects, which levels, and over how many sessions. Vague answers stop there.

Subject depth is tested through the assessment, not the syllabus. A DP Chemistry applicant is asked how they would guide a student whose internal assessment has a weak research question but good data. Someone who has genuinely supervised IAs answers that quickly and concretely. Someone who has not, talks about topics.

Communication is assessed too, because a tutor who cannot explain a student's weakness to a parent in plain language becomes a monthly source of friction.

After placement, the first weeks matter more than the file. If sessions are being rescheduled repeatedly, if there is no visible plan, or if the student cannot say what last week's session was about, the match is reviewed and changed. Requesting a change does not require justification beyond "this is not working".

contentBlocks.heading: Honest limits of IB tutoring in Orchid Petals, Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Some things tutoring does not fix, and saying so early saves money.

A student who starts specialist DP support eight weeks before a final session will improve, but the improvement is bounded by what can be re-learned in eight weeks. Nobody can promise a grade, and any tutor who does should be dropped from your list immediately.

A second limit: if the student does not want the tutor, the sessions become a supervised study hour. That is sometimes still worth paying for, but be honest with yourself about what you are buying. Bringing the student into the first conversation, even briefly, changes the outcome more than any screening step we run.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week make sense for a DP student before mocks?

For two weak subjects, resist the urge to run four sessions a week alongside school and activities. Something gets dropped, and it is usually sleep. contentBlocks.heading: What online IB tutoring does better for Puri Diplomatic Greens families
contentBlocks.body:
Start with the part that gets undersold. An online session gives you a shared screen, and a shared screen is a better teaching surface than a dining table for most Diploma Programme work. A marked Paper 2 script can be annotated live while the student watches the marker's logic unfold. A Physics diagram can be redrawn three times in ninety seconds. A spreadsheet of internal assessment data can be interrogated by both people at once, with the raw numbers visible rather than described.

Online also removes the geography problem, which for this address is the real problem. Puri Diplomatic Greens sits on the Dwarka Expressway side, and the density of experienced IB tutors here is thinner than in the older parts of the city. Searching only for someone who can drive over narrows the pool badly. Searching for someone who has taught your exact subject at your exact level widens it enormously.

And sessions can be recorded, which matters more than parents expect. A student revising in April can rewatch the February explanation of a topic they thought they had understood.

Now the other side, because it is real. Online is weaker where presence does the teaching. It is weaker for young children. It is weaker for a student who has learned to look attentive while thinking about nothing.

contentBlocks.heading: PYP, MYP and DP support near Puri Diplomatic Greens, Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Support across Grade 1 to Grade 12 breaks into three quite different jobs.

Primary Years Programme work is about protecting curiosity while quietly building fluency in reading and number. Parents from this belt often ask for worksheet packs. We usually push back, because a PYP child drilled early tends to arrive in Middle Years Programme unable to handle an open-ended task. Two short sessions a week, in person where possible, do more.

Middle Years Programme support is largely translation work. The student understands photosynthesis; the student cannot write about photosynthesis in a way that satisfies Criterion B. Personal Project supervision in Grade 10 is another common request, and it is worth starting before the proposal is submitted rather than after the first supervisor meeting goes badly.

Diploma Programme work is where most enquiries from Sector 99 to Sector 109 land. Internal assessment planning, Extended Essay supervision, Theory of Knowledge structure, and timed past-paper practice for the May 2026 and November 2026 sessions. Younger DP cohorts benefit from planning earlier than the school calendar suggests, particularly for the Extended Essay, where a research question chosen in a rush costs marks quietly for eight months.

DP: IA planning, EE supervision, TOK structure, timed papers

When a tutor is already based in these sectors, home sessions work well and often extend across neighbouring towers, since one evening trip can cover two students in the same cluster.

contentBlocks.heading: Economics, English A and the writing-heavy subjects at Puri Diplomatic Greens
contentBlocks.body:
Enquiries from this cluster skew towards the subjects where marks are lost in writing rather than in calculation.

Economics is the clearest example. A student can define price elasticity perfectly and still score poorly, because the marks sit in an accurate diagram, a correctly labelled axis shift, and an evaluation paragraph that genuinely argues against its own first half. The internal assessment commentaries need current news articles chosen with judgement, which is a skill worth teaching directly rather than leaving to chance.

English A rewards a different discipline. The unseen commentary is not a comprehension exercise. It asks for a reading of a short passage that is defensible line by line, and students who write generalised essays about themes without quoting closely plateau early.

On the quantitative side, an IB maths tutor Puri Diplomatic Greens request should always specify Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, and the level. Physics and Chemistry requests should mention whether the immediate need is content, laboratory work, or the internal assessment write-up, because those three call for different people.

One caution: a tutor who is comfortable across five subjects is usually not deeply strong in any of them.

A home tutor wins when attention is the problem rather than understanding. Sitting beside a student changes behaviour in a way a video call does not. Pauses get noticed. A wrong turn in a calculation is caught at the point it happens, not three lines later when the student says nothing is working.

Home sessions also win for practical subject work: physical lab notebooks, hand-drawn graphs, past papers written under exam conditions with someone in the room enforcing the clock.

For IB home tuition Puri Diplomatic Greens the constraint is supply. Fewer experienced IB tutors live in the Sector 99 to Sector 109 stretch than in older Gurugram, so home matches here depend more on luck of timing than in Sohna Road or the DLF phases.

A workable compromise many families use: one home session at the weekend for the subject that needs presence, and midweek online sessions for the rest. faqs.question: Is it harder to find a home tutor here than in older parts of Gurugram?
faqs.answer: Generally yes. The Dwarka Expressway sectors filled with residents faster than they filled with experienced IB tutors, so the pool willing and able to reach Sector 102 or Sector 108 on a weekday evening is smaller than in the DLF phases or along Sohna Road. Matches do happen, particularly where a tutor already teaches another student in Sobha City or a neighbouring tower. But if home tutoring is your only acceptable format, expect fewer names and a longer wait, and treat availability as something to confirm rather than assume.

faqs.question: Can sessions be recorded so my child can revise from them later?
faqs.answer: Online sessions can generally be recorded when both the tutor and the family agree to it, and for Diploma Programme subjects this turns out to be genuinely useful. A topic explained carefully in October is rarely retained perfectly by March, and rewatching the original explanation is faster than rebuilding it from notes. Discuss it at the introductory session rather than starting to record afterwards. Some tutors prefer to share written summaries instead, which works nearly as well and takes less of the student's revision time to review.

faqs.question: My son has a two-hour round trip to school. When should sessions be scheduled?
faqs.answer: Late evening is the worst slot for hard content, and many families here learn that the expensive way. A student home at 4:30 pm after an early bus has limited capacity for new Physics or Higher Level Maths at 7:30 pm. The pattern that tends to hold: put the hardest subject on a Saturday or Sunday morning when the mind is fresh, and keep weekday evenings for revision, doubt-solving, and reviewing marked work. Shorter weekday sessions, done consistently, beat long ones that get skipped.

faqs.question: What is the difference between IA support and Extended Essay supervision?
faqs.answer: They are different jobs with different timelines. Internal assessment support is subject-bound and usually intense over a few weeks: research question, method, data, analysis, evaluation, all within one subject's criteria. Extended Essay supervision runs for the better part of a year and is closer to research mentoring, covering scope control, source quality, argument structure and the reflection sessions. A tutor strong at one is not automatically strong at the other, and they are often priced separately because the work continues between sessions in both cases.

faqs.question: How do I know a tutor genuinely knows IB and not just the subject?
faqs.answer: Ask a process question, not a content question. Something like: how would you help a student whose Economics commentary uses a good article but the wrong diagram. Or: what would you change first in an internal assessment with clean data and a weak research question. A tutor who has done this work answers concretely and quickly. A subject expert with no IB experience will talk about the topic instead of the criteria. You can ask this yourself during the introductory session.

faqs.question: Do you support Personal Project work in Grade 10?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the timing of the request matters. Personal Project supervision is most useful before the proposal is finalised, because an over-ambitious project is difficult to rescue later without abandoning months of work. A tutor helps most by narrowing the scope, structuring the process journal from the start rather than reconstructing it at the end, and keeping the criteria visible while the work happens. contentBlocks.heading: This week, this month, this term: deciding on a tutor at Raheja Atlantis
contentBlocks.body:
Parents rarely start looking for a tutor at a calm moment. The trigger is usually a report, a teacher's comment, or a draft that came back covered in corrections. So the decision gets made under time pressure, and time pressure produces bad matches.

Break it into three horizons and it becomes manageable.

This week, settle only two things: the exact subject and level, and whether a tutor travelling to your tower is realistic given the hours you can offer. Everything else can wait. Getting these two wrong is what causes a restart in November.

This month, run an introductory session and hold the tutor to a specific diagnosis. Not "needs to practise more". Something like: struggles to structure an evaluation paragraph, or reads the command term but answers a different question. Then set a plan for four sessions, and look at one piece of marked work at the end of it.

This term, judge the arrangement on whether the shape of the work has changed. Grades move slowly and unevenly. Structure, timing and self-diagnosis move faster, and they are the leading indicators.

Useful ordering, because it protects you from paying for six months of pleasant, directionless sessions.

Month one: demand a specific diagnosis, not general encouragement
Term one: judge on structure and timing before grades

The settled nature of the area helps. Requests for IB tuition near Raheja Atlantis are more often fillable as home sessions than requests from the far edges of Gurugram.

contentBlocks.heading: Choosing home or online IB tuition in Raheja Atlantis, Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Both formats are available and the choice should follow the student, not the parent's preference.

Pick home sessions when the student needs someone in the room to stay on task, when the work is physical (lab notebooks, hand-drawn graphs, timed papers under supervision), or when the child is young enough that a screen becomes the most interesting object available. Because this pocket is well served, an IB home tutor Raheja Atlantis request has a reasonable chance of being filled for a fixed weekday slot.

Pick online when the subject is narrow. A Higher Level subject with few takers, or a specific internal assessment methodology, needs the right person more than it needs a nearby person. Online also survives disruption better: exam season, illness, a parent's travel, a sudden change in school timings.

There is a cost to online that nobody advertises. The tutor sees less. Small signs of confusion that a person sitting beside a student catches instantly can pass unnoticed on a video call for several minutes.

Many families here run both formats across a week, and there is nothing untidy about that. The format should serve the subject, and different subjects want different things.

contentBlocks.heading: Chemistry, Physics and the deadlines that arrive first
contentBlocks.body:
In the Diploma Programme, science internal assessments tend to land before students feel ready, and that single fact drives a large share of the enquiries from this area.

Chemistry causes the most trouble. The experiment is usually fine. The research question is too broad, the variables are not properly controlled, and the uncertainty treatment is thin, so a report with decent data scores in the middle. A tutor who has supervised these before will restructure the question in the first session, which is worth more than six sessions of content revision.

Physics splits differently. Students often manage the mathematics and lose marks on explanation questions, where a stated law needs applying to the specific situation described rather than recited.

For an IB science tutor Raheja Atlantis request, say which of the three problems you have: content gaps, laboratory work, or the write-up.

Maths requests should specify Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, plus Higher or Standard Level, since the exploration and the teaching differ substantially. Economics and English A support is also commonly requested, and both reward a tutor who marks work closely rather than discussing it in general terms.

Here is the sequence, day by day, so the wait is predictable.

Day one: an advisor calls. The conversation covers programme, subject, level, school, what the last marked piece looked like, and which time windows are genuinely free. If home sessions are wanted, the block and preferred start time are recorded.

Day five onwards: the introductory session, scheduled around school timings.

The timeline stretches when the request is unusual. A rare Higher Level combination at a fixed evening slot can take longer, and everything remains subject to tutor availability in that week.

contentBlocks.heading: A term-by-term view of PYP, MYP and DP in Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Support runs from Grade 1 to Grade 12, and each programme has its own rhythm across the year.

In the Primary Years Programme, the useful measure is not marks at all. It is whether a child reads for longer than they did three months ago, and whether number work is done without visible dread. Progress here is slow and worth being patient with. Frequent short sessions beat long ones.

In the Middle Years Programme, the year turns around assessed tasks and, in Grade 10, the Personal Project. Students who understand the material still lose marks by writing outside the criteria, so the term's work is largely about learning what each criterion is asking for and answering that instead.

The Diploma Programme calendar is the least forgiving. Grade 11 sets up the internal assessments and the Extended Essay question. Grade 12 is dominated by drafts, mocks, and timed practice for the May 2026 and November 2026 sessions. Starting Extended Essay support in Grade 11, before the question is locked, is the difference between editing an argument and rescuing one.

Cohorts entering the Diploma Programme later would do well to plan earlier than the school calendar implies.

contentBlocks.heading: The checks behind every IB tutor list in Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Screening is a set of steps, and it is worth knowing what they do and do not cover.

Identity and background details are collected and confirmed before a tutor is proposed for a home visit. Qualifications are checked against the subject claimed. Teaching history is checked against the programme, and applicants who describe their experience loosely are asked to state the programme, subjects, levels and the number of students taught. Answers that stay general end the conversation there.

The depth check is an assessment scenario. A Diploma Programme Physics applicant may be asked what they would do with an internal assessment whose data is fine but whose analysis has no meaningful uncertainty discussion. Experience shows up in the speed and specificity of the answer.

The part that is often skipped elsewhere: whether the tutor can explain a student's difficulty to a parent in ordinary words. A tutor who cannot do that leaves you guessing every month.

What screening does not do is predict chemistry between a tutor and a particular teenager. That only shows in the first weeks, which is why the match is reviewed early and can be changed on request.

contentBlocks.heading: What four weeks of tutoring near Raheja Atlantis can and cannot change
contentBlocks.body:
Expectations set correctly at the start prevent most disappointments later.

In four weeks, a well-matched tutor can change how a student approaches a question, tighten the structure of written answers, fix a specific misconception that has been quietly costing marks, and get one piece of coursework onto a better footing. Those are real, observable outcomes.

In four weeks, no tutor can cover two years of missed foundations, guarantee any grade or points total, or make a student want the subject. Anyone who suggests otherwise is worth walking away from, however confident they sound.

There are limits on this end too. Availability for particular Higher Level subjects at particular hours varies week by week, and can be reviewed only when you ask. A tutor's schedule may change mid-term. Home sessions in this pocket are more often fillable than in newer parts of the city, but they are never guaranteed in advance.

And one uncomfortable point worth naming: if a student attends sessions but does nothing between them, tutoring becomes an expensive supervised hour. That is worth knowing before the third month, not after it.

faqs.question: How quickly can a tutor start if the deadline is three weeks away?
faqs.answer: For common subjects at Standard Level, a first session within about a week is usually achievable, sometimes faster. For a specific Higher Level subject at a fixed evening hour, it can take longer, because the constraint is the intersection of subject depth and a free slot. If the deadline is genuinely three weeks out, say so on the first call and consider accepting an online match to start immediately, then reviewing the format once the immediate crisis has passed. faqs.question: Is a tutor from Malibu Towne or Suncity likely to be available for home sessions?

faqs.question: Should we choose a tutor who teaches at an IB school?
faqs.answer: It helps, though it is not the deciding factor and it can create a complication. Someone currently teaching the programme knows the criteria and the pace well. But a teacher at your child's own school may face a conflict of interest around marking their own student's work, which schools take seriously. What matters more is direct experience with the assessment: internal assessments supervised, Extended Essays guided, past papers marked. Ask about that record specifically rather than asking only where they teach.

faqs.question: My daughter is doing well but wants to move from a 5 to a higher grade. Is tutoring worth it?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and the work looks different from remedial tutoring. A student at that level rarely has content gaps. The marks sit in evaluation, in precision of language, in reading command terms accurately, and in finishing papers within the time allowed. A tutor for this student spends most sessions on marked work rather than on teaching new material. No specific grade can be promised by anyone, but this kind of refinement work tends to show results faster than foundation-building does.

faqs.question: Can one tutor handle both Physics and Chemistry at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Some can, and you should test the claim rather than take it. Ask about the internal assessment in each subject separately, since the demands differ: Chemistry work often turns on variable control and uncertainty, Physics on modelling and explanation. A tutor genuinely strong in both will answer both questions with equal specificity. If one answer is noticeably thinner, take that subject to a second tutor. Two focused matches usually outperform one convenient one, even though it means managing two schedules.

faqs.question: How long should each session be for a Grade 11 student?
faqs.answer: Sixty to ninety minutes suits most Diploma Programme subjects. Below an hour, there is barely time to review previous work and teach something new. Beyond ninety minutes, attention drops for a student who has already sat through a full school day, and the last half hour tends to be wasted. Longer weekend sessions can work when the focus is a timed paper or internal assessment work that needs a continuous stretch. Ask what the tutor plans to do with the time rather than only what it costs.

faqs.answer: No. IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform. The same applies to the schools named on this page: they are mentioned because students living nearby attend them and because their deadlines affect tutoring plans, not because any relationship exists between them and this platform.

faqs.question: What should we ask the tutor at the end of the first month?
faqs.answer: Three questions work well. What is the single biggest thing costing marks right now, in one sentence. What has changed since the first session. What is the plan for the next four weeks, specifically. A tutor with a real grip on the student answers all three without hesitation. Answers that stay at the level of effort and confidence, with nothing concrete about the work itself, suggest the sessions have drifted into supervised homework, and that is the moment to intervene.

faqs.question: Can we pause sessions during school exams and resume later?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is a common request during school assessment weeks or family travel. Tell the advisor and the tutor early, because a tutor holding a fixed evening slot may fill it if the pause runs long, and resuming afterwards then depends on availability again. Some families keep one shorter weekly session running through the break instead of stopping fully, which preserves the slot and keeps the student in the habit. Either arrangement is workable; the difference is what happens to your timing.

But a teacher at your child's own school may face a conflict of interest around marking their own student's work, which schools take seriously. What matters more is direct experience with the assessment: internal assessments supervised, Extended Essays guided, past papers marked. Ask about that record specifically rather than asking only where they teach.

mainEntity.name: My daughter is doing well but wants to move from a 5 to a higher grade. Is tutoring worth it?

acceptedAnswer.text: Often yes, and the work looks different from remedial tutoring. A student at that level rarely has content gaps. The marks sit in evaluation, in precision of language, in reading command terms accurately, and in finishing papers within the time allowed. A tutor for this student spends most sessions on marked work rather than on teaching new material. No specific grade can be promised by anyone, but this kind of refinement work tends to show results faster than foundation-building does.

mainEntity.name: Can one tutor handle both Physics and Chemistry at Higher Level?

acceptedAnswer.text: Some can, and you should test the claim rather than take it. Ask about the internal assessment in each subject separately, since the demands differ: Chemistry work often turns on variable control and uncertainty, Physics on modelling and explanation. A tutor genuinely strong in both will answer both questions with equal specificity. If one answer is noticeably thinner, take that subject to a second tutor. Two focused matches usually outperform one convenient one, even though it means managing two schedules.

mainEntity.name: How long should each session be for a Grade 11 student?

acceptedAnswer.text: Sixty to ninety minutes suits most Diploma Programme subjects. Below an hour, there is barely time to review previous work and teach something new. Beyond ninety minutes, attention drops for a student who has already sat through a full school day, and the last half hour tends to be wasted. Longer weekend sessions can work when the focus is a timed paper or internal assessment work that needs a continuous stretch. Ask what the tutor plans to do with the time rather than only what it costs.

mainEntity.name: Does IB Gram have any tie-up with Raheja Atlantis or its management?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform. This page exists to serve families who live in and around Raheja Atlantis, and no connection with the society, its residents welfare association or its management is claimed or implied. The same applies to the schools named on this page: they are mentioned because students living nearby attend them and because their deadlines affect tutoring plans, not because any relationship exists between them and this platform.

mainEntity.name: What should we ask the tutor at the end of the first month?

acceptedAnswer.text: Three questions work well. What is the single biggest thing costing marks right now, in one sentence. What has changed since the first session. What is the plan for the next four weeks, specifically. A tutor with a real grip on the student answers all three without hesitation. Answers that stay at the level of effort and confidence, with nothing concrete about the work itself, suggest the sessions have drifted into supervised homework, and that is the moment to intervene.

mainEntity.name: Can we pause sessions during school exams and resume later?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, and it is a common request during school assessment weeks or family travel. Tell the advisor and the tutor early, because a tutor holding a fixed evening slot may fill it if the pause runs long, and resuming afterwards then depends on availability again. Some families keep one shorter weekly session running through the break instead of stopping fully, which preserves the slot and keeps the student in the habit. Either arrangement is workable; the difference is what happens to your timing.

finalCta: Give an advisor the programme and grade, the subject and level, the next school deadline and two workable slots. You will get a short list with fee bands, a straight answer about home sessions at your block, and a diagnostic first session. Nothing is committed until you have seen how that session goes.
