contentBlocks.heading: What a Tutor Near Vipul Greens Should Refuse to Promise
contentBlocks.body:
A few statements should end a conversation rather than start one.

Any promise of a specific grade. No tutor can commit to a 7, a two-point rise or a fixed total, because the result depends on a student's starting point, the work done between sessions and how much of the course is still ahead. A confident number is a sales technique.

Any claim of affiliation with a school. IB Gram is an independent platform. It is not connected to any school, and it is not connected to Vipul Greens, its management or its residents' association. Nobody here has an arrangement with the society, and any tutor implying otherwise is misrepresenting the position.

Any claim to have inside knowledge of examination content. That does not exist.

There is also a limit worth stating from our side. Tutoring works on a student who will do something between sessions. Where the real issue is attendance, sleep, or a child who has quietly disengaged from school altogether, a weekly hour is the wrong tool and adding a second one makes the week heavier without making it better. In those cases the school counsellor is a more useful call than we are.
items: No grade, score or percentage improvement is ever promised

contentBlocks.heading: The Checks Behind Every Name Sent to a Gurugram Home
contentBlocks.body:
Verification runs before an introduction, and it covers four things.

Identity, confirmed against a government photo identity document. Qualification, checked against the specific subject and level requested rather than the subject alone, which is the check that catches an otherwise excellent mathematician being proposed for the wrong Higher Level course. Teaching history, taken with detail: which syllabus versions, which levels, which assessment components actually supervised. And references, followed up rather than merely collected, with extra attention for anyone who will be teaching inside a home.

The interview is the part that does the real work. Candidates are not asked to explain a topic, because most can. They are asked to look at a piece of student writing and justify the level it earns against a published criterion, then say what feedback they would give. Someone who has genuinely marked IB work answers that quickly and specifically. Someone who has only studied the syllabus does not.

None of this predicts rapport. A tutor can pass every check and still be wrong for one particular teenager, which is why the first two sessions function as a trial and why asking for a change at that point is treated as routine rather than as a complaint about anyone.

Do one thing before you contact anybody, including us. Find the most recent report card and the last marked assignment, and read the teacher comments properly rather than looking only at the levels. faqs.question: What is the honest short answer to whether we need an IB tutor at all?
faqs.answer: If the last report shows a level or predicted grade that has moved down, or teacher comments repeating the same skill word across terms, a tutor is likely to help. If the marks are steady and the complaint is boredom or motivation, extra hours usually make things worse rather than better. A single subject with one weak unit often needs six to eight sessions, not a year of tuition. We would rather tell you that than sell a longer arrangement that the evidence does not support.

faqs.question: Should we hand over the school report and teacher comments before the first session?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it makes a noticeable difference. A tutor who has seen criterion levels or a marked script arrives with a hypothesis instead of spending the first hour discovering what everyone already knew. Share whatever you are comfortable sharing, and remove personal details if you prefer. The most useful single item is not the report card but a recent piece of work with the teacher's annotations still on it. That shows precisely where marks were lost, which a summary grade never does.

faqs.question: Our school gives MYP criterion levels rather than percentages. Can a tutor work from those?
faqs.answer: That is the format tutors actually prefer. A criterion level out of eight tells you which skill has failed, not just that a subject went badly. A student at 6 on knowledge and 3 on communicating has a writing and structure problem, and the sessions should look nothing like those for a student with the reverse pattern. Ask any prospective tutor to explain what your child's specific spread suggests. Their answer will tell you within a minute whether they have taught the Middle Years Programme or only read about it.

faqs.question: The predicted grade in Physics dropped two points this term. How worried should we be?
faqs.answer: Worried enough to act this term, not enough to panic. Predicted grades move for several reasons: a hard topic, a missed assessment, a change in how strictly a teacher is marking as the course gets closer to the real thing. Ask the subject teacher what drove the change before booking anything. If the answer names a topic, that is a content gap and it is fixable. If the answer is about examination technique under timed conditions, that is a different tutor and a shorter piece of work.

faqs.question: Is IB Gram connected to Vipul Greens or its residents' association in any way?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform with no arrangement, endorsement or affiliation involving Vipul Greens, its management, its residents' association or any facility inside it. The society is named on this page only because families living in and around it search for tutoring nearby, and because travel times within the Sector 48-50 belt affect what can realistically be scheduled. Any tutoring arrangement is directly between the family and the tutor, and any society permissions for a visitor remain the family's own to arrange.

faqs.question: Does the tutor come to the flat, and who arranges gate entry?
faqs.answer: Home sessions take place wherever the family chooses within their own residence, subject to tutor availability for that slot. Visitor entry is entirely the family's arrangement with their own society, following whatever process applies there. We do not hold any standing permission and would not claim one. In practice families share the tutor's name and phone number with their gate in advance, which avoids the ten minutes of confusion that otherwise eats into a first session. Online sessions sidestep the question altogether.

faqs.question: Is an online session priced differently from one at home?
faqs.answer: Usually, yes. Fees are set by individual tutors and generally reflect subject, level, experience and travel, so a home session that involves driving into the Sohna Road belt at peak hour often carries more than the same hour delivered online. The gap varies and should be discussed openly before you book. A split arrangement, with one session at home and one online each week, is a common middle path for families who want in-person teaching without paying travel into every hour.

faqs.question: My daughter never asks questions in class. Does one-to-one actually change that?
faqs.answer: Frequently, though not instantly. In a class of twenty-four, a quiet student can pass an entire term without ever admitting confusion, and the report will simply record a flat level. One to one removes the audience, which is the main barrier for most such students. Expect two or three sessions before questions start coming, and tell the tutor about this at the outset so they build in pauses rather than talking for fifty minutes. If nothing shifts by session four, the tutor's manner may be the wrong fit.

faqs.question: What evidence should we look at before renewing for a second month?
faqs.answer: Look at the next marked piece of school work, not at how the sessions felt. Specifically, check whether the errors the tutor said they were addressing have stopped appearing. A student can enjoy every session and still repeat the same mistake, which means the diagnosis was wrong rather than the tutor lazy. Also watch for the student bringing a specific doubt to a session unprompted. That habit tends to appear before the marks move and is a reliable early sign that the arrangement is working.

mainEntity.name: What is the honest short answer to whether we need an IB tutor at all?

acceptedAnswer.text: If the last report shows a level or predicted grade that has moved down, or teacher comments repeating the same skill word across terms, a tutor is likely to help. If the marks are steady and the complaint is boredom or motivation, extra hours usually make things worse rather than better. A single subject with one weak unit often needs six to eight sessions, not a year of tuition. We would rather tell you that than sell a longer arrangement that the evidence does not support.

mainEntity.name: Should we hand over the school report and teacher comments before the first session?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, and it makes a noticeable difference. A tutor who has seen criterion levels or a marked script arrives with a hypothesis instead of spending the first hour discovering what everyone already knew. Share whatever you are comfortable sharing, and remove personal details if you prefer. The most useful single item is not the report card but a recent piece of work with the teacher's annotations still on it. That shows precisely where marks were lost, which a summary grade never does.

mainEntity.name: Our school gives MYP criterion levels rather than percentages. Can a tutor work from those?

acceptedAnswer.text: That is the format tutors actually prefer. A criterion level out of eight tells you which skill has failed, not just that a subject went badly. A student at 6 on knowledge and 3 on communicating has a writing and structure problem, and the sessions should look nothing like those for a student with the reverse pattern. Ask any prospective tutor to explain what your child's specific spread suggests. Their answer will tell you within a minute whether they have taught the Middle Years Programme or only read about it.

mainEntity.name: The predicted grade in Physics dropped two points this term. How worried should we be?

acceptedAnswer.text: Worried enough to act this term, not enough to panic. Predicted grades move for several reasons: a hard topic, a missed assessment, a change in how strictly a teacher is marking as the course gets closer to the real thing. Ask the subject teacher what drove the change before booking anything. If the answer names a topic, that is a content gap and it is fixable. If the answer is about examination technique under timed conditions, that is a different tutor and a shorter piece of work.

mainEntity.name: Is IB Gram connected to Vipul Greens or its residents' association in any way?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform with no arrangement, endorsement or affiliation involving Vipul Greens, its management, its residents' association or any facility inside it. The society is named on this page only because families living in and around it search for tutoring nearby, and because travel times within the Sector 48-50 belt affect what can realistically be scheduled. Any tutoring arrangement is directly between the family and the tutor, and any society permissions for a visitor remain the family's own to arrange.

mainEntity.name: Does the tutor come to the flat, and who arranges gate entry?

acceptedAnswer.text: Home sessions take place wherever the family chooses within their own residence, subject to tutor availability for that slot. Visitor entry is entirely the family's arrangement with their own society, following whatever process applies there. We do not hold any standing permission and would not claim one. In practice families share the tutor's name and phone number with their gate in advance, which avoids the ten minutes of confusion that otherwise eats into a first session. Online sessions sidestep the question altogether.

mainEntity.name: Is an online session priced differently from one at home?

acceptedAnswer.text: Usually, yes. Fees are set by individual tutors and generally reflect subject, level, experience and travel, so a home session that involves driving into the Sohna Road belt at peak hour often carries more than the same hour delivered online. The gap varies and should be discussed openly before you book. A split arrangement, with one session at home and one online each week, is a common middle path for families who want in-person teaching without paying travel into every hour.

mainEntity.name: My daughter never asks questions in class. Does one-to-one actually change that?

acceptedAnswer.text: Frequently, though not instantly. In a class of twenty-four, a quiet student can pass an entire term without ever admitting confusion, and the report will simply record a flat level. One to one removes the audience, which is the main barrier for most such students. Expect two or three sessions before questions start coming, and tell the tutor about this at the outset so they build in pauses rather than talking for fifty minutes. If nothing shifts by session four, the tutor's manner may be the wrong fit.

mainEntity.name: What evidence should we look at before renewing for a second month?

acceptedAnswer.text: Look at the next marked piece of school work, not at how the sessions felt. Specifically, check whether the errors the tutor said they were addressing have stopped appearing. A student can enjoy every session and still repeat the same mistake, which means the diagnosis was wrong rather than the tutor lazy. Also watch for the student bringing a specific doubt to a session unprompted. That habit tends to appear before the marks move and is a reliable early sign that the arrangement is working.
